2027-01-01.title: Mary, the Holy Mother of God · Solemnity · Octave Day of Christmas
readings: The Lord bless you and keep you
May God be gracious to us and bless us
God sent his Son, born of a woman
Mary treasured all these words; the child was named Jesus
2027-01-01.alt: Holy day of obligation in many countries (check your diocese). World Day of Prayer for Peace. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-01-01.verse: But Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart.
theo: The Church begins the civil year not with fireworks but with a mother. On the eighth day of Christmas she proclaims the oldest Marian title of all: Mary is Theotokos, Mother of God. The Council of Ephesus (431) defended this title against those who wished to call her only the mother of the man Jesus. The Church answered: the child she bore is one Person, the eternal Son, true God and true man; so she is truly the Mother of God (CCC 495). To honour Mary is to confess who Jesus is.

St Paul gives the shortest Christmas creed in the New Testament: “when the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman, born under the law.” God's eternity enters time through the yes of one woman. And the purpose is our adoption: “so that we might receive adoption as children.” Because of Mary's Son, the Spirit cries in our hearts, “Abba! Father!” The first reading puts the priestly blessing of Aaron on our lips for the new year: “The LORD bless you and keep you.” In Christ that blessing has a face.

In the Gospel the shepherds find “Mary and Joseph, and the child lying in the manger.” Everyone is amazed, “But Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart.” On the eighth day the child is circumcised and receives the name Jesus, “the name given by the angel”. The year opens with a Name that means “the Lord saves”, and with a mother who keeps God's deeds in her heart. St Paul VI made this day the World Day of Peace; Mary, Queen of Peace, teaches us to receive the Prince of Peace.
conn: Theotokos.
Greek for “God-bearer”. The Council of Ephesus (431) proclaimed it; the people of Ephesus carried the bishops through the streets with torches in joy (CCC 466, 495).
The priestly blessing.
Numbers 6:24–26 is the oldest biblical text found outside the Bible: two small silver scrolls from about 600 BC found at Ketef Hinnom in Jerusalem carry these words.
The eighth day.
Circumcision on the eighth day (Genesis 17:12; Leviticus 12:3) brought a boy into the covenant. Jesus, born under the Law, keeps it faithfully in order to redeem those under the Law.
The Name.
Yeshua means “the LORD saves” (Matthew 1:21). Every knee bends at this name (Philippians 2:10). The Church keeps the Most Holy Name of Jesus as an optional memorial on 3 January.
World Day of Peace.
St Paul VI instituted it in 1968. Each year the Pope publishes a message for 1 January.
Pondering.
The Greek word in Luke 2:19 means “to throw together”: Mary puts events side by side and seeks their meaning in God. She is the model of meditation on the Word.
altar: At the altar we receive the same Body that Mary carried in her womb and held in her arms. Each Communion makes us, in a small way, bearers of God.
The priest ends Mass with a blessing. Today let it echo the blessing of Aaron: the Lord bless you and keep you through this whole year.
outline: Ask: how did you begin the new year? With whom?
Mary's title protects the truth about Jesus.
Born of a woman so that we may cry Abba.
The Lord bless you and keep you.
Mary pondering by the manger while the shepherds go out praising.
live: Begin the year with a blessing (Numbers 6:24–26)
Parents, bless each child tonight with the words of Aaron.
Ponder like Mary (Luke 2:19)
Keep a small notebook this year: one line each day on what God did.
Pray for peace
Pray one decade of the Rosary today for peace in the world and in your family.
Honour the Name
Bow your head each time you say or hear the name of Jesus.
fathers: St Cyril of Alexandria
If anyone does not confess that Emmanuel is truly God, and that the holy Virgin is therefore Mother of God, for she bore according to the flesh the Word of God made flesh, let him be anathema.
St Ambrose (in substance)
Mary is the type of the Church: virgin and mother, she bore Christ, as the Church brings forth children by water and the Spirit.
magis: Mary is truly Theotokos, Mother of God.
Mary, Mother of God and of the Church, model of faith and charity.
1 January restored as the solemnity of Mary's divine motherhood.
Mary, Mother of God and Mother of the Church.
saints: 2 Jan: Sts Basil the Great and Gregory Nazianzen. 3 Jan: Epiphany of the Lord (in India). 7 Jan: St Raymond of Penyafort.
2027-01-01.prayer: O God, who through the fruitful virginity of Blessed Mary bestowed on the human race the grace of eternal salvation, grant, we pray, that we may experience the intercession of her, through whom we were found worthy to receive the author of life, our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son. Who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen.

2027-01-03.title: The Epiphany of the Lord · Solemnity
readings: The glory of the Lord has risen upon you
Every nation on earth will adore you, Lord
We observed his star and have come to pay him homage
2027-01-03.alt: In India and many other countries the Epiphany is kept on the Sunday between 2 and 8 January. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-01-03.verse: When they saw that the star had stopped, they were overwhelmed with joy. On entering the house, they saw the child with Mary his mother; and they knelt down and paid him homage. Then, opening their treasure chests, they offered him gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
theo: Epiphany means “manifestation”. At Christmas the Lord was revealed to the shepherds of Israel; today he is revealed to the nations, represented by the Magi from the East. Isaiah saw it centuries before: “Arise, shine; for your light has come… Nations shall come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your dawn.” Camels from Midian and Sheba bring “gold and frankincense”. St Paul names the mystery hidden for ages: “the Gentiles have become fellow heirs, members of the same body, and sharers in the promise in Christ Jesus.” Today is the feast of all of us who are not descended from Abraham, and who have been brought into God's family.

The Magi follow a star; they read the book of creation honestly, and it leads them to Jerusalem. There they need the Scriptures to find the exact place: Bethlehem, as the prophet Micah wrote. Reason and revelation work together. Yet the scribes who knew the Scriptures did not take the few hours' walk to Bethlehem, and Herod, who heard the same news, felt threatened and planned murder. The same Christ draws some to worship and provokes others to fear. Knowledge without worship leaves us where we are.

“They knelt down and paid him homage.” The journey ends in adoration. The gifts became, in the Fathers, a confession of faith: gold for a king, frankincense for God, myrrh for one who would die (St Irenaeus, St Gregory the Great). And “they left for their own country by another road.” Whoever truly meets Christ cannot go back the same way. The Church in India, born from the faith of the Apostle Thomas and the missions of Francis Xavier, is itself a fruit of the Epiphany: the light reached the East.
conn: Who were the Magi?

Probably astrologer-priests from Persia or Babylon. Tradition later counted three (from the three gifts) and called them kings (from Psalm 72:10–11 and Isaiah 60:3). The names Caspar, Melchior and Balthasar appear in the sixth century.
The star.
Numbers 24:17 had foretold: “a star shall come out of Jacob.” Whatever its natural explanation, Matthew presents it as God speaking to the nations in their own language.
Bethlehem.
Micah 5:2 names Bethlehem of Judah, David's town, as the birthplace of the ruler of Israel. The chief priests and scribes quote it to Herod.
Three manifestations.

The ancient Church celebrates three epiphanies together: the Magi, the Baptism in the Jordan and the wedding at Cana (antiphon of the Magnificat). The Eastern Churches put the Baptism at the centre (Denha).
Announcing Easter.
On the Epiphany the deacon or cantor may proclaim the date of Easter and the movable feasts. In 2027 Easter falls on 28 March, and Ash Wednesday on 10 February.
Chalk blessing.
In many places doors are marked with 20 + C + M + B + 27: the initials of the Magi, and also of Christus mansionem benedicat, may Christ bless this house.
altar: The Magi brought gold, frankincense and myrrh. At the offertory we bring bread and wine, and with them our lives. God gives back his Son.
Like the Magi we kneel before the same Child, now hidden under the sign of bread, and we too return home by another road.
outline: Ask: have you ever followed a sign that led you somewhere unexpected?
The nations come to the light; we are the Gentiles who have been invited.
Point 2 · Seeking with star and Scripture
Reason and revelation lead the Magi; the scribes stay home.
The journey ends in worship and begins a new life.
Three travellers kneeling in a poor house before a child and his mother.
“They left for their own country by another road.”
live: Bless your home
Mark your door with chalk: 20 + C + M + B + 27, and pray for all who enter.
Bring a gift (Matthew 2:11)
Offer Christ one concrete gift this week: time, money for the poor, a habit given up.
Seek him honestly
Read one chapter of a Gospel each day this month, like the Magi searching.
Pray for the missions
Pray for those who do not yet know Christ, and support the Holy Childhood or a mission collection.
fathers: St Leo the Great (in substance)
Let all peoples come and adore their Creator: the Magi stand for the whole multitude of the nations who are to believe.
St Peter Chrysologus (in substance)
The Magi offered gold to the king, incense to God and myrrh to the one who was to die.
magis: The Epiphany: the great multitude of the nations enters the family of the patriarchs.
Christ the light of the nations; all are called to the people of God.
The pilgrim Church is missionary by her very nature.
The Magi as men of restless hearts seeking God.
saints: 4 Jan: Christmas weekday. 7 Jan: St Raymond of Penyafort. 10 Jan: Baptism of the Lord.
2027-01-03.prayer: O God, who on this day revealed your Only Begotten Son to the nations by the guidance of a star, grant in your mercy that we, who know you already by faith, may be brought to behold the beauty of your sublime glory. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen.

2027-01-06.title: 6 January · Wednesday after the Epiphany
readings: Every nation on earth will adore you, Lord
Take heart, it is I; do not be afraid
2027-01-06.alt: Christmas weekday. In countries where the Epiphany is not transferred to Sunday, today is the Solemnity of the Epiphany; the Eastern Churches celebrate the Baptism of the Lord (Denha). Liturgical colour: white.
2027-01-06.verse: There is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear; for fear has to do with punishment, and whoever fears has not reached perfection in love.
theo: After feeding the five thousand, Jesus sends the disciples ahead by boat and goes up the mountain to pray. In the night the wind is against them and they strain at the oars. Early in the morning he comes to them walking on the sea. They think he is a ghost and cry out in terror. Then comes one of the most beautiful sentences in the Gospels: “Take heart, it is I; do not be afraid.” In Greek, “it is I” is egō eimi, the name God revealed to Moses. He climbs into the boat, and the wind ceases.

Mark adds an honest note: “they did not understand about the loaves, but their hearts were hardened.” They had just seen a miracle and still did not see who Jesus was. St John gives the remedy for fear: “There is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear.” God's love living in us, and our love for one another, is the only lasting answer to the storms of life. “No one has ever seen God; if we love one another, God lives in us.”
outline: Ask: what are you most afraid of this year?
Jesus on the mountain sees them straining.
God's love in us is the answer.
“Take heart, it is I; do not be afraid.”
live: Name your fear
Tell Jesus in prayer the one fear that troubles you most this year.
Love casts out fear (1 John 4:18)
Do one act of love today toward someone you are afraid of or avoid.
2027-01-06.prayer: Lord Jesus, you saw your disciples straining at the oars and came to them across the sea. When the wind is against me, let me hear your voice: Take heart, it is I. Fill me with your perfect love that casts out fear. Amen.
altar: At Mass, after the Our Father, the priest prays that we may be “safe from all distress”. Christ steps into the boat of our lives in Holy Communion.

2027-01-10.title: The Baptism of the Lord · Feast
readings: Here is my servant, in whom my soul delights
The Lord will bless his people with peace
God anointed Jesus with the Holy Spirit and with power
You are my Son, the Beloved
2027-01-10.alt: Year B alternatives: Isaiah 55:1–11; Isaiah 12; 1 John 5:1–9. The Christmas season ends today; Ordinary Time begins tomorrow. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-01-10.verse: And a voice came from heaven, “You are my Son, the Beloved; with you I am well pleased.”
theo: The Christmas season closes at the river Jordan. Mark tells it with few words and great force. John proclaims: “The one who is more powerful than I is coming after me… I have baptized you with water; but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit.” Then Jesus comes from Nazareth and is baptised. As he comes up out of the water, “he saw the heavens torn apart and the Spirit descending like a dove on him.” The Father speaks: “You are my Son, the Beloved; with you I am well pleased.”

Isaiah had described this Servant: “Here is my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen, in whom my soul delights; I have put my spirit upon him.” He will not shout or break a bruised reed; he will bring justice and be “a light to the nations, to open the eyes that are blind.” In Acts, Peter tells the household of Cornelius how “God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and with power; how he went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil.” The anointing at the Jordan is the beginning of the Christ's public mission, and Peter's sermon shows it reaching the Gentiles.

Jesus had no sin to wash away. He went down into the water in solidarity with sinners and to sanctify the waters for our Baptism (CCC 536, 1224). What the Father said to Jesus, he says to each of us in Baptism: you are my beloved child. The torn heavens are not closed again; through Christ, heaven is open to us. Today is a good day to renew our baptismal promises and to live as people anointed by the Spirit for doing good.
conn: Torn apart.
Mark uses the strong verb schizō: the heavens are “torn apart”. He uses it again only once, for the Temple curtain at Jesus' death (Mark 15:38). The way to God is opened at the Jordan and at Calvary.
The Servant Songs.
Isaiah 42:1–4 is the first of four Servant Songs (Isaiah 42, 49, 50, 52–53). The Father's words at the Jordan echo Isaiah 42:1 and Psalm 2:7.
The dove.
The Spirit hovering over the waters at creation (Genesis 1:2) and the dove returning to Noah's ark (Genesis 8:11) stand behind this sign: a new creation begins.
Cornelius.
Peter's sermon in Acts 10 is preached to a Roman centurion's household. The Spirit falls on Gentiles, and they are baptised: the Jordan's grace reaches the nations.
Christ, the Anointed.
“Christ” (Greek) and “Messiah” (Hebrew) mean Anointed. At the Jordan Jesus is anointed with the Spirit for his mission (Acts 10:38; CCC 438).
End of Christmas.
The Christmas season ends with this feast. Tomorrow the Church begins Ordinary Time, following the public life of Jesus Sunday by Sunday.
altar: At the Jordan the Spirit came down on Jesus. At the altar the priest calls down the same Spirit on the bread and wine (the epiclesis), and they become the Body and Blood of Christ.
Our Baptism made us members of Christ's Body; the Eucharist nourishes that life. Font and altar belong together.
outline: Ask: do you know the date and place of your Baptism?
Isaiah's gentle Servant, a light to the nations.
The Spirit and the Father's voice.
What the Father says to us.
Jesus coming up out of the water under an open sky.
live: Renew your Baptism
At Mass today renew your baptismal promises with full attention; at home, light your baptismal candle if you have it.
Find your baptismal date
Ask your parents or parish and write the date in your diary.
Do good (Acts 10:38)
Like Jesus who went about doing good, do one deliberate act of kindness each day this week.
Holy water
Bless yourself with holy water when you enter and leave church.
fathers: St Gregory Nazianzen
Christ is bathed in light; let us also be bathed in light. Christ is baptised; let us also go down with him, that we may also rise with him.
St Maximus of Turin
Christ is baptised not to be made holy by the water, but to make the water holy.
magis: Christ's Baptism and the Church's Baptism.
Know the date of your Baptism and celebrate it.
saints: 13 Jan: St Hilary. 14 Jan: St Devasahayam (in India). 17 Jan: St Antony, abbot (Sunday this year).
2027-01-10.prayer: Almighty ever-living God, who, when Christ had been baptised in the River Jordan and as the Holy Spirit descended upon him, solemnly declared him your beloved Son, grant that your children by adoption, reborn of water and the Holy Spirit, may always be well pleasing to you. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen.

2027-01-17.title: Second Sunday in Ordinary Time
readings: Speak, for your servant is listening
Here am I, Lord; I come to do your will
Your bodies are members of Christ
Come and see; we have found the Messiah
2027-01-17.alt: Year B. The memorial of St Antony, abbot, is not kept this year because it falls on Sunday. Liturgical colour: green.
2027-01-17.verse: He said to them, “Come and see.” They came and saw where he was staying, and they remained with him that day. It was about four o'clock in the afternoon.
theo: After the Epiphany and the Baptism, the first Sundays of Ordinary Time show how people come to Jesus. John the Baptist sees Jesus walk by and says, “Look, here is the Lamb of God!” Two of his disciples follow. Jesus turns and asks the first question he speaks in John's Gospel: “What are you looking for?” They answer with another question: “Rabbi… where are you staying?” And he says: “Come and see.” They stay with him that day; John even remembers the hour, “about four o'clock in the afternoon”. An encounter with Jesus is never forgotten.

Andrew immediately finds his brother Simon: “We have found the Messiah.” He brings him to Jesus, who looks at him and gives him a new name: “You are to be called Cephas”, Peter, rock. Faith spreads from person to person, brother to brother. The first reading shows the boy Samuel learning to recognise God's call, thanks to old Eli: “Speak, LORD, for your servant is listening.” Every vocation needs someone who helps us hear.

St Paul reminds the Corinthians that this following involves the whole person: “your bodies are members of Christ… your body is a temple of the Holy Spirit… glorify God in your body.” Discipleship is not only ideas; it is where we go, what we do with our bodies, whom we stay with. The Psalm puts the answer on our lips: “Here I am… I delight to do your will.”
conn: The Lamb of God.
John the Baptist's title for Jesus recalls the Passover lamb (Exodus 12) and the Servant led like a lamb (Isaiah 53:7). The priest repeats it before Communion.
First words.
Jesus' first words in John are a question: “What are you looking for?” (1:38). His first words to Mary Magdalene after the Resurrection are similar: “Whom are you looking for?” (20:15).
Four o'clock.
Literally “the tenth hour”. The precise detail suggests the memory of an eyewitness, perhaps the unnamed second disciple, traditionally John.
Andrew.
Andrew appears three times in John, always bringing someone to Jesus: Peter, the boy with the loaves (6:8–9), and the Greeks (12:20–22). He is the patron of missionaries.
Cephas.
The Aramaic kepha means rock; Greek Petros. A new name means a new mission, as with Abraham and Israel.
Samuel and Eli.
Samuel had not yet experienced the LORD; Eli, though weak as a father, recognised God's call and taught the boy to answer. God works even through imperfect guides.
altar: Before Communion the priest says the Baptist's words: “Behold the Lamb of God.” Like the first disciples, we come and see, and stay with him.
Our bodies are members of Christ. In Communion his Body joins ours, and we leave to glorify God in our bodies.
outline: Ask: what are you really looking for in life?
Samuel learns to listen with Eli's help.
Point 2 · What are you looking for?
Point 4 · We have found the Messiah
Two young men walking with Jesus at four in the afternoon.
live: Answer the question (John 1:38)
Write down honestly: what am I looking for? Then bring it to Jesus in prayer.
Stay with him
Spend fifteen minutes this week before the Blessed Sacrament.
Be an Andrew (John 1:41)
Invite one person to Mass or to a prayer group.
Be an Eli
Help a young person discern God's call; pray for vocations.
fathers: St Augustine (in substance)
They asked where he lived, and he said: Come and see. Let us also make a dwelling in our heart where he may come and teach us.
St John Chrysostom (in substance)
Andrew did not keep the treasure to himself, but hurried to share it with his brother.
magis: Samuel's prayer: “Speak, for your servant is listening.”
Our bodies, temples of the Holy Spirit.
Pope Benedict XVI, Deus Caritas Est 1
Being Christian begins with an encounter with a Person.
saints: 18–25 Jan: Week of Prayer for Christian Unity. 20 Jan: Sts Fabian and Sebastian. 21 Jan: St Agnes. 24 Jan: St Francis de Sales (Sunday this year).
2027-01-17.prayer: Almighty ever-living God, who govern all things, both in heaven and on earth, mercifully hear the pleading of your people and bestow your peace on our times. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen.

2027-01-24.title: Third Sunday in Ordinary Time · Sunday of the Word of God
readings: The people of Nineveh turned from their evil ways
Lord, make me know your ways
The present form of this world is passing away
Repent and believe in the good news; follow me
2027-01-24.alt: Year B. Sunday of the Word of God, established by Pope Francis in 2019 (Aperuit illis). The memorial of St Francis de Sales is not kept this year because it falls on Sunday. Week of Prayer for Christian Unity. Liturgical colour: green.
2027-01-24.verse: Now after John was arrested, Jesus came to Galilee, proclaiming the good news of God, and saying, “The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has come near; repent, and believe in the good news.”
theo: Mark's Gospel moves fast. John the Baptist is arrested, and Jesus begins at once: “The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has come near; repent, and believe in the good news.” These are the first words of Jesus in Mark, a summary of all his preaching. The time of waiting is over; God's reign is here in person. Two responses are asked: repent, which means turn around and change your mind; and believe, which means trust and give yourself to the good news.

Then the call: Jesus sees Simon and Andrew casting their nets and says, “Follow me and I will make you fish for people.” “And immediately they left their nets and followed him.” James and John leave their father Zebedee in the boat with the hired men. The word of Jesus is not information but a power that changes lives. Jonah's short sermon in Nineveh shows the same power: “the people of Nineveh believed God”, and God relented. Paul adds urgency: “the appointed time has grown short… the present form of this world is passing away.” We cannot hold this world's goods as if they were final.

Today is the Sunday of the Word of God. Pope Francis asked the whole Church to celebrate, study and spread the Scriptures on this day, recalling St Jerome: “Ignorance of the Scriptures is ignorance of Christ.” The word that called the first disciples by the Sea of Galilee calls us through the Bible. Let us enthrone the Scriptures in our homes and read them daily.
conn: The time is fulfilled.
The Greek word is kairos, God's decisive moment, not ordinary clock time (chronos).
Repent.
Metanoia means a change of mind and heart, a turning around of the whole person (CCC 1430–1431).
Fishers of people.
The prophets used fishing for God's gathering of people (Jeremiah 16:16); Jesus turns it into a mission of rescue.
Immediately.
Mark uses this word over forty times; the Kingdom demands a prompt response.
Sunday of the Word of God.
Instituted by Pope Francis on 30 September 2019 in the apostolic letter Aperuit illis, for the Third Sunday in Ordinary Time each year.
Week of Prayer for Christian Unity.
Ends tomorrow, on the feast of the Conversion of St Paul.
altar: At every Mass the Church sets two tables: the table of the word and the table of the Body of Christ (Dei Verbum 21). Today we honour the first with special care.
The Christ who called the fishermen by the lake comes to us in the Eucharist and calls us again: follow me.
outline: Ask: what would make you leave your job today to follow someone?
Empty nets left on the shore.
“Repent, and believe in the good news.”
live: Enthrone the Bible
Place the Bible in a place of honour at home, with a lamp or flowers.
Read daily
Begin reading Mark's Gospel, one passage each day.
Leave one net (Mark 1:18)
Name one attachment that keeps you from following Jesus, and let it go.
Pray for unity
Pray for Christian unity on the last days of the Unity Week.
fathers: St Jerome
Ignorance of the Scriptures is ignorance of Christ.
St Gregory the Great (in substance)
The fishermen left little, a boat and nets, but they left everything, because they left even the desire to possess.
magis: The Church venerates the Scriptures as she venerates the Body of the Lord; the faithful should read them often.
Pope Francis institutes the Sunday of the Word of God.
Benedict XVI on the prayerful reading of Scripture (lectio divina).
Christ the one Word of Scripture; conversion.
saints: 25 Jan: Conversion of St Paul (feast). 26 Jan: Sts Timothy and Titus. 27 Jan: St Angela Merici. 28 Jan: St Thomas Aquinas. 31 Jan: Fourth Sunday (St John Bosco not kept).
2027-01-24.prayer: Almighty ever-living God, direct our actions according to your good pleasure, that in the name of your beloved Son we may abound in good works. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. Let us also pray: Lord Jesus, you call us as you called Simon and Andrew: give us hearts that repent and believe, hands that leave the nets that hold us, and a love for your word that reads it daily and lives it gladly. Amen.

2027-01-31.title: Fourth Sunday in Ordinary Time
readings: I will raise up a prophet and put my words in his mouth
O that today you would listen to his voice! Harden not your hearts
He taught them as one having authority
2027-01-31.alt: Year B. The memorial of St John Bosco is not kept this year because it falls on Sunday. Tomorrow begins February; 2 February is the Presentation of the Lord. Liturgical colour: green.
2027-01-31.verse: They were astounded at his teaching, for he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.
theo: Moses, near the end of his life, gives Israel a promise: “The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people; you shall heed such a prophet.” At Sinai the people had been terrified of hearing God's voice directly, so God says: “I will put my words in the mouth of the prophet, who shall speak to them everything that I command.” Israel waited for centuries for this prophet like Moses. The Gospel shows him walking into the synagogue at Capernaum.

On the Sabbath Jesus teaches, and the people are “astounded at his teaching, for he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.” The scribes quoted others; Jesus speaks with his own voice: “But I say to you.” Then a man with an unclean spirit cries out: “What have you to do with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are, the Holy One of God.” Jesus rebukes him: “Be silent, and come out of him!” and the spirit leaves. The people ask: “What is this? A new teaching—with authority! He commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey him.” His word does what it says.

The Psalm gives the response: “O that today you would listen to his voice! Do not harden your hearts.” Paul encourages the Corinthians to “unhindered devotion to the Lord”, praising those who give themselves wholly to God in celibacy, while honouring marriage as a true calling. Whatever our state of life, the question is the same: do we let the authoritative word of Jesus free us from what binds us? Today we would have honoured St John Bosco, who freed countless young people from the street through the word, education and love of Christ.
conn: A prophet like Moses.
Peter (Acts 3:22) and Stephen (Acts 7:37) apply Deuteronomy 18:15 to Jesus.
Authority.
Greek exousia: power that comes from one's own being. The scribes cited rabbis; Jesus speaks as the Lawgiver.
The Holy One of God.
The demon knows Jesus' identity before the disciples do; but knowledge without love is not faith (James 2:19).
The messianic secret.
Jesus silences the demons; he will reveal himself in his own way, on the cross.
Capernaum.
Jesus' base in Galilee; the remains of a synagogue stand there today, built over an earlier one.
St John Bosco.
Priest of Turin (1815–1888), founder of the Salesians, whose schools and youth centres serve many in Kerala.
altar: At Mass the same authoritative word is proclaimed, and then the Word made flesh gives himself to us.
Before Communion we say: Lord, I am not worthy… but only say the word, and my soul shall be healed. We trust the power of his word.
outline: Ask: whose voice has real authority in your life?
A synagogue in silence after the shout.
“O that today you would listen to his voice!”
live: Listen today (Psalm 95:7)
Spend five minutes in silence with today's Gospel.

Bring one bondage or addiction to Jesus in confession.
Pray for vocations
Pray for priests, religious and consecrated people.
Honour Don Bosco
Do something kind for a young person in difficulty.
fathers: St Jerome (in substance)
The demon confesses Christ but is rebuked: truth from a lying mouth is not welcome; let the Lord be confessed by those who love him.
St Bede (in substance)
The people were amazed at the new teaching; his authority was shown not only in words but in works.

Jesus' signs and the defeat of Satan's reign.
Virginity for the Kingdom and marriage, both gifts of the Lord.
Celibacy as a gift and a sign.

2027-01-31.prayer: Grant us, Lord our God, that we may honour you with all our mind, and love everyone in truth of heart. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. Let us also pray: Lord Jesus, Holy One of God, you teach with authority and free those who are bound. Speak to us today, let us not harden our hearts, and make us bearers of your freeing word to the young. Amen.

2027-01-02.title: 2 January · Saints Basil the Great and Gregory Nazianzen, Bishops and Doctors · Memorial
readings: Let what you heard from the beginning abide in you
All the ends of the earth have seen the victory of our God
I am the voice of one crying out in the wilderness
2027-01-02.verse: John answered them, “I baptize with water. Among you stands one whom you do not know, the one who is coming after me; I am not worthy to untie the thong of his sandal.”
theo: The priests and Levites ask John the Baptist, “Who are you?” He answers first with what he is not: not the Messiah, not Elijah, not the prophet. Then he says who he is: “I am the voice of one crying out in the wilderness.” A voice exists for a word. John's whole identity is to point to another: “Among you stands one whom you do not know.” Humility is not thinking little of ourselves; it is knowing that our life is for Christ.

St John warns that whoever denies the Son does not have the Father, and urges: “Let what you heard from the beginning abide in you.” Today we honour two friends who defended that faith from the beginning: St Basil the Great and St Gregory Nazianzen, students together in Athens, monks together, then bishops in Cappadocia. Against the Arians they defended the full divinity of the Son and of the Holy Spirit; the Creed we say on Sundays owes much to them. Gregory wrote of their friendship: we knew only two roads, the one to the church and the one to the schools.
outline: Ask: if someone asked “Who are you?”, what would you answer?
Point 1 · A voice for the Word
Point 2 · Abide in what you heard
Faithful to the faith of the Apostles.
Basil and Gregory: friends who led each other to God.
“Among you stands one whom you do not know.”
live: Make way for Christ (John 1:23)
In one conversation today, point to Christ rather than to yourself.
Thank God for a friend
Pray for a friend who has helped your faith.
2027-01-02.prayer: O God, who were pleased to give light to your Church by the example and teaching of the Bishops Saints Basil and Gregory, grant that in humility we may learn your truth and practise it faithfully in charity. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
altar: At the altar the priest, like John, says “Behold the Lamb of God”: he points away from himself to Christ.

2027-01-04.title: 4 January · Monday after the Epiphany
readings: Test the spirits to see whether they are from God
I will give you the nations for your inheritance
The people who sat in darkness have seen a great light
2027-01-04.alt: Christmas weekday after the Epiphany. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-01-04.verse: From that time Jesus began to proclaim, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near.”
theo: After the Epiphany the Gospel shows the light moving out into the world. Jesus leaves Nazareth and settles in Capernaum, in “Galilee of the Gentiles”, a border land mixed with pagans. Matthew sees Isaiah fulfilled: “the people who sat in darkness have seen a great light.” The first word of his preaching is “Repent”, turn around, because the kingdom has come near. Then he goes through Galilee teaching, proclaiming and curing “every disease and every sickness”, and crowds come even from the Decapolis and beyond the Jordan.

St John gives a rule for discernment: “do not believe every spirit, but test the spirits.” The test is Christ: every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is from God. Many voices offer light today; not all lead to the Light. And John adds a word of courage to the small community: “the one who is in you is greater than the one who is in the world.”
outline: Ask: what does a dark room feel like when someone switches on the light?
Jesus begins in a mixed, despised region.
The first word of the kingdom.
Christ in the flesh is the measure.
“Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near.”
live: Turn around (Matthew 4:17)
Name one habit that turns you away from God and take one step back today.
Test the voices (1 John 4:1)
Before sharing a religious message on WhatsApp, check it against the teaching of the Church.
2027-01-04.prayer: Lord Jesus, light of the nations, you began your preaching in Galilee of the Gentiles. Shine into the dark places of my life, turn my heart back to you, and teach me to recognise your Spirit. Amen.
altar: Each Mass begins with a call to repentance: “Let us acknowledge our sins.” We answer the first word of Jesus' preaching before we receive the Bread of life.

2027-01-05.title: 5 January · Tuesday after the Epiphany
readings: Every nation on earth will adore you, Lord
He had compassion for them; the loaves are multiplied
2027-01-05.alt: Christmas weekday after the Epiphany. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-01-05.verse: In this is love, not that we loved God but that he loved us and sent his Son to be the atoning sacrifice for our sins.
theo: St John writes the three words that sum up the Bible: “God is love.” He does not say only that God loves, but that love is what God is: the eternal exchange of Father, Son and Spirit. And he shows where we see it: “not that we loved God but that he loved us and sent his Son.” Love begins with God, not with us. Our love is always an answer.

Mark shows that love in action. Jesus sees a great crowd, and “he had compassion for them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd.” First he feeds them with his word; then, when evening comes, he feeds them with bread. The disciples want to send the people away; Jesus says, “You give them something to eat.” Five loaves and two fish, blessed, broken and given, become enough for five thousand, with twelve baskets left over. The words he uses, took, blessed, broke, gave, are the words of the Last Supper. Every Eucharist is this compassion of the Shepherd.
outline: Ask: when did someone notice your need before you asked?
live: Share bread (Mark 6:37)
Give a meal or groceries to a family in need this week.
Answer love (1 John 4:10)
Thank God for one way he loved you first.
2027-01-05.prayer: Lord Jesus, Good Shepherd, you had compassion on the hungry crowd. Take my five loaves and two fish, bless them and use them for others, and teach me to love as you have loved me. Amen.
altar: At every Mass the priest takes the bread, blesses, breaks and gives. The miracle of the loaves continues: the Shepherd feeds his flock with himself.

2027-01-07.title: 7 January · Thursday after the Epiphany
readings: Whoever loves God must love his brother also
Every nation on earth will adore you, Lord
Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing
2027-01-07.alt: Optional memorial: St Raymond of Penyafort, priest. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-01-07.verse: Then he began to say to them, “Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.”
theo: Jesus returns to Galilee “filled with the power of the Spirit” and goes to the synagogue of Nazareth on the sabbath. He is handed the scroll of Isaiah and reads: “The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor.” Then he rolls up the scroll, sits down, and says: “Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.” The Anointed One, the Christ, is standing in front of them. His mission is good news for the poor, release for captives, sight for the blind, freedom for the oppressed, a year of the Lord's favour.

St John draws the consequence for us: “We love because he first loved us.” And he forbids a split between love of God and love of neighbour: “those who do not love a brother or sister whom they have seen, cannot love God whom they have not seen.” Faith that is born of God “conquers the world”. St Raymond of Penyafort, a Dominican of Barcelona, compiled the Church's laws and was a great confessor; he helped found the Mercedarians, who ransomed Christian captives. He lived the programme of Nazareth: freedom for prisoners, mercy for sinners.
outline: Ask: what would change if God's word were fulfilled “today” in your life?
Jesus is the Christ, the Anointed.
God's word is not only for the past.
Point 3 · Love the brother you see
Love of God and neighbour cannot be split.
“Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.”
live: Good news to the poor (Luke 4:18)
Visit, help or speak kindly to one poor person today.
Love the one you see (1 John 4:20)
Make peace with a family member you have been cold towards.
2027-01-07.prayer: Lord Jesus, anointed by the Spirit, you brought good news to the poor and freedom to captives. Let your word be fulfilled today in my life, and teach me to love the brother and sister I see, so that I may truly love God whom I do not see. Amen.
altar: In the Liturgy of the Word Christ himself speaks when the Scriptures are read (Sacrosanctum Concilium 7). Each Mass is a “today” of his word.

2027-01-08.title: 8 January · Friday after the Epiphany
readings: Whoever has the Son has life
Lord, if you choose, you can make me clean
2027-01-08.alt: Christmas weekday after the Epiphany. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-01-08.verse: Then Jesus stretched out his hand, touched him, and said, “I do choose. Be made clean.” Immediately the leprosy left him.
theo: A man “covered with leprosy” sees Jesus, falls on his face and begs: “Lord, if you choose, you can make me clean.” He has no doubt about Jesus' power; he only asks about his will. And Jesus answers with a touch before a word. To touch a leper was forbidden and made a person unclean. But here holiness is contagious, not uncleanness: “I do choose. Be made clean.” Then Jesus sends him to the priest, so that he may be restored to the community.

Luke adds that the news spread and crowds came, “But he would withdraw to deserted places and pray.” Power and prayer go together in Jesus. St John speaks of three witnesses, “the Spirit and the water and the blood”, and of the testimony of God: “God gave us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. Whoever has the Son has life.” The Fathers saw in the water and blood the sacraments of Baptism and the Eucharist, by which Christ still touches and heals us.
outline: Ask: is there something in your life you feel too ashamed to bring to Jesus?
Faith in his power, trust in his will.
Point 3 · Whoever has the Son has life
live: Bring your leprosy
Bring to confession the sin you are most ashamed of.
Touch the untouchable
Visit a patient no one visits, or greet someone others avoid.
2027-01-08.prayer: Lord Jesus, if you choose, you can make me clean. Stretch out your hand and touch what is broken in me. Let me never be ashamed to come to you, and let me bring your healing touch to others. Amen.
altar: The words before Communion echo the leper's faith: “Lord, I am not worthy… but only say the word and my soul shall be healed.”

2027-01-09.title: 9 January · Saturday after the Epiphany
readings: If we ask anything according to his will, he hears us
The Lord takes delight in his people
He must increase, but I must decrease
2027-01-09.alt: Christmas weekday after the Epiphany. Liturgical colour: white. Saturday memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary is not kept in the Christmas season.
2027-01-09.verse: He who has the bride is the bridegroom. The friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices greatly at the bridegroom's voice. For this reason my joy has been fulfilled. He must increase, but I must decrease.
theo: John the Baptist's disciples are upset: everyone is now going to Jesus. John answers with one of the most generous sentences in the Bible. He calls Jesus the Bridegroom, the title God used for himself with Israel, and calls himself only “the friend of the bridegroom”, who rejoices to hear his voice. “For this reason my joy has been fulfilled. He must increase, but I must decrease.” Jealousy in ministry and in families is overcome by joy that Christ is loved.

St John ends his letter with confidence in prayer: “if we ask anything according to his will, he hears us.” He asks us to pray for a brother who sins, and he closes with a short warning: “Little children, keep yourselves from idols.” An idol is anything we put in God's place: money, reputation, a person, our own importance. The Baptist's way, letting Christ grow and ourselves grow smaller, is the surest protection against idols. Tomorrow we celebrate the Baptism of the Lord, where John's ministry reaches its high point.
outline: Ask: how do you feel when someone else gets the credit?
Jesus is God's spouse for his people.
The joy of the best man.
“He must increase, but I must decrease.”
live: Rejoice in others' gifts (John 3:29)
Praise sincerely someone whose success you envy.
Name your idol (1 John 5:21)
Ask: what takes God's place in my life? Give it back to him.
2027-01-09.prayer: Lord Jesus, Bridegroom of the Church, let me rejoice to hear your voice. May you increase in my life and I decrease. Keep me from idols, and teach me to ask according to your will. Amen.
altar: The Church is the bride, and the Eucharist is the wedding feast of the Lamb (Revelation 19:9). At each Mass the Bridegroom gives himself to his bride.

2027-01-11.title: Monday of the First Week in Ordinary Time
readings: God has spoken to us by a Son
Let all his angels worship him
Follow me and I will make you fish for people
2027-01-11.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 1 (Year I). Liturgical colour: green.
2027-01-11.verse: and saying, “The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has come near; repent, and believe in the good news.”
theo: Ordinary Time begins with two great openings. The Letter to the Hebrews starts: “Long ago God spoke to our ancestors in many and various ways by the prophets, but in these last days he has spoken to us by a Son.” The prophets were many voices; the Son is God's final Word, “the reflection of God's glory and the exact imprint of God's very being”, greater than the angels. In these weeks we will read Hebrews slowly, learning who Christ is and what he has done.

Mark's Gospel opens Jesus' preaching with four short phrases: “The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has come near; repent, and believe in the good news.” Then, walking by the Sea of Galilee, Jesus sees two pairs of brothers at work and says: “Follow me and I will make you fish for people.” Immediately they leave nets, boat and father. Ordinary Time is not dull time; it is the time of following Jesus day by day in ordinary life.
outline: Ask: what does “ordinary” mean in Ordinary Time?
Point 1 · God has spoken by a Son
The final Word of the Father.
“Follow me and I will make you fish for people.”
live: Read Mark
Read Mark's Gospel from the beginning, one section a day, during these weeks.
Leave one net (Mark 1:18)
Name one thing that holds you back from following Jesus more closely, and let it go today.
2027-01-11.prayer: Lord Jesus, eternal Word of the Father, you call ordinary people at their work. Speak to me in these ordinary days, give me a heart that repents and believes, and help me to leave my nets and follow you. Amen.
altar: At every Mass the Word who spoke through the prophets now speaks in the Gospel, and then gives himself in the Eucharist.

2027-01-12.title: Tuesday of the First Week in Ordinary Time
readings: Crowned with glory because of the suffering of death
You have given your Son rule over the works of your hands
He taught them as one having authority
2027-01-12.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 1 (Year I). Liturgical colour: green.
2027-01-12.verse: They were astounded at his teaching, for he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.
theo: In the synagogue of Capernaum Jesus teaches, and the people are astounded: “he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.” The scribes quoted earlier teachers; Jesus speaks with his own authority, as the Lawgiver himself. Then a man with an unclean spirit cries out, “I know who you are, the Holy One of God.” Jesus silences him with a word and sets the man free. His word is not only true; it is powerful.

Hebrews quotes Psalm 8: “What are human beings that you are mindful of them?” God made us a little lower than the angels and crowned us with glory. But we do not yet see everything subject to us. “But we do see Jesus, who for a little while was made lower than the angels, now crowned with glory and honor because of the suffering of death.” He shared our flesh, and “Jesus is not ashamed to call them brothers and sisters.” The one who speaks with authority is also our brother.
outline: Ask: whose words have authority in your life?
Point 3 · Our brother crowned with glory
Not ashamed to call us brothers and sisters.
“He taught them as one having authority.”
live: Let his word have authority
Choose one teaching of Jesus you have been ignoring and obey it today.
Pray for deliverance
Pray for those bound by addiction or evil influences.
2027-01-12.prayer: Lord Jesus, Holy One of God, your word has authority over every evil. Speak with authority in my life, set me free from what binds me, and let me live as your brother or sister, crowned with your glory. Amen.
altar: In the Mass Jesus speaks with authority in the Gospel, and with the same authority says over the bread: This is my Body.

2027-01-13.title: Wednesday of the First Week in Ordinary Time
readings: He had to become like his brothers and sisters in every respect
The Lord remembers his covenant for ever
He cured many; in the morning he went out to pray
2027-01-13.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 1 (Year I). Liturgical colour: green. Optional memorial: St Hilary, bishop and doctor.
2027-01-13.verse: In the morning, while it was still very dark, he got up and went out to a deserted place, and there he prayed.
theo: Mark shows us a full day in the life of Jesus. After the synagogue he enters Simon's house, where Simon's mother-in-law lies sick with fever. “He came and took her by the hand and lifted her up. Then the fever left her, and she began to serve them.” Healing becomes service. At sunset the whole town crowds at the door, and Jesus cures many. Then, “In the morning, while it was still very dark, he got up and went out to a deserted place, and there he prayed.” The secret of his day is his night prayer.

Hebrews explains why the Son came so close: he shared our flesh and blood “so that through death he might destroy the one who has the power of death, that is, the devil, and free those who all their lives were held in slavery by the fear of death.” He became like us in every respect to be a merciful high priest. “Because he himself was tested by what he suffered, he is able to help those who are being tested.” St Hilary of Poitiers, a married convert who became bishop, defended the divinity of Christ in exile; he knew both trials and the Lord who helps in them.
outline: Ask: what does a full day of yours look like? Where does God fit?
He was tested and can help us.
live: Rise for prayer (Mark 1:35)
Give the first ten minutes of tomorrow morning to prayer before checking your phone.
Healed to serve (Mark 1:31)
After any blessing you receive this week, serve someone in thanks.
2027-01-13.prayer: Lord Jesus, you took Simon's mother-in-law by the hand and lifted her up, and before dawn you prayed to your Father. Lift me up from what weighs me down, teach me to pray, and help me in every test, for you were tested as I am. Amen.
altar: Jesus' prayer before dawn flows into every Mass, where he prays to the Father for us. We join his prayer and are lifted up to serve.

2027-01-14.title: Thursday of the First Week in Ordinary Time
readings: Today, if you hear his voice
If today you hear his voice, harden not your hearts
Moved with pity, Jesus touched him
2027-01-14.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 1 (Year I). Liturgical colour: green. In India: St Devasahayam, martyr (check the diocesan calendar).
2027-01-14.verse: Moved with pity, Jesus stretched out his hand and touched him, and said to him, “I do choose. Be made clean!”
theo: Hebrews takes up Psalm 95: “Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as in the rebellion.” The generation in the wilderness saw God's works for forty years and still hardened their hearts. The warning is urgent: “exhort one another every day, as long as it is called ‘today,’ so that none of you may be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.” Faith is kept alive day by day, and we are responsible for one another.

In Mark a leper comes to Jesus and kneels: “If you choose, you can make me clean.” Mark notes that Jesus was “moved with pity”, a word for a compassion felt in the depths of the body. He touches the man and heals him. Then a striking reversal: the healed man spreads the news, and Jesus “could no longer go into a town openly, but stayed out in the country.” The leper comes back into town, and Jesus takes his place outside. In India today many remember St Devasahayam, a court official who embraced Christ and, rejecting caste barriers, mixed freely with people of every community; arrested for his faith, he was executed in 1752. He too went outside the camp with Jesus.
outline: Ask: when did compassion move you to act?
The healed man returns; Jesus stays outside.
live: Encourage someone today (Hebrews 3:13)
Send a message of faith and encouragement to someone struggling.
Cross a barrier
Spend time with someone others exclude, as Jesus and St Devasahayam did.
2027-01-14.prayer: Lord Jesus, moved with pity you touched the leper and took his place outside. Today let me hear your voice and not harden my heart. Through the prayers of St Devasahayam, give me courage to love across every barrier. Amen.
altar: Hebrews says Jesus suffered outside the city gate (Hebrews 13:12). At the altar we meet the One who went outside for us.

2027-01-15.title: Friday of the First Week in Ordinary Time
readings: Let us make every effort to enter that rest
Do not forget the works of the Lord
The Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins
2027-01-15.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 1 (Year I). Liturgical colour: green.
2027-01-15.verse: When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, “Son, your sins are forgiven.”
theo: The house in Capernaum is so full that four men cannot bring their paralysed friend to Jesus. So they climb onto the roof, dig through it and lower him down on his mat. Mark says: “When Jesus saw their faith”, the faith of the four friends, he spoke to the paralytic. And his first words surprise everyone: “Son, your sins are forgiven.” Jesus goes first to the deepest paralysis, sin. The scribes object: who can forgive sins but God alone? They are right about God, and wrong about Jesus.

To show that “the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”, Jesus tells the man to take up his mat and walk, and he does. Everyone is amazed: “We have never seen anything like this!” Hebrews speaks of the “rest” God promised, which the wilderness generation failed to enter through unbelief, and urges: “Let us therefore make every effort to enter that rest.” Forgiveness is the beginning of that rest. In the sacrament of Reconciliation Christ still says: your sins are forgiven; rise and walk.
outline: Ask: who are the four friends who have carried you to Jesus?
Faith that does not give up.
live: Carry a friend (Mark 2:3)
Bring someone to Jesus this week: by prayer, an invitation to Mass or a visit.
Receive forgiveness
Go to confession before the end of the month.
2027-01-15.prayer: Lord Jesus, you saw the faith of four friends and forgave the paralysed man. Thank you for those who have carried me to you. Forgive my sins, raise me up, and let me carry others to you. Amen.
altar: Before Communion we pray: “Lord, I am not worthy… but only say the word.” The One who forgave the paralytic speaks the same word to us.

2027-01-16.title: Saturday of the First Week in Ordinary Time
readings: The word of God is living and active
Your words, Lord, are Spirit and life
I have come to call not the righteous but sinners
2027-01-16.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 1 (Year I). Liturgical colour: green. In India: St Joseph Vaz, priest (check the diocesan calendar). Optional: Saturday memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary.
2027-01-16.verse: Indeed, the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing until it divides soul from spirit, joints from marrow; it is able to judge the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
theo: Hebrews offers two images side by side. First, the word of God is “living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword”: it reaches the hidden places of the heart and lays everything bare. That could frighten us. But immediately comes the second image: “we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but we have one who in every respect has been tested as we are, yet without sin. Let us therefore approach the throne of grace with boldness.” The word that sees everything leads us to the mercy that forgives everything.

Mark shows this in action. Jesus sees Levi sitting at the tax booth, a collaborator despised by his people, and says: “Follow me.” Levi gets up and follows, and soon Jesus is eating at his table with “many tax collectors and sinners”. The Pharisees are shocked. Jesus answers: “Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick; I have come to call not the righteous but sinners.” The Church is first a hospital for sinners, and every one of us is a patient called to follow.
outline: Ask: when has a word of Scripture cut to your heart?
“I have come to call not the righteous but sinners.”
live: Let the word read you (Hebrews 4:12)
Read today's Gospel slowly and ask: what does it reveal in my heart?
Eat with sinners (Mark 2:16)
Share a meal or tea with someone others look down on.
2027-01-16.prayer: Lord Jesus, your word is living and sees my heart, and you are a high priest who understands my weakness. Call me again as you called Levi, heal me as the doctor of sinners, and let me approach your throne of grace with confidence. Amen.
altar: At Mass the word of God is proclaimed, and then the Physician of souls feeds us at his table. Like Levi's guests, we come as sinners and are welcomed.

2027-01-18.title: Monday of the Second Week in Ordinary Time
readings: He learned obedience through what he suffered
You are a priest for ever, in the line of Melchizedek
2027-01-18.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 2 (Year I). Liturgical colour: green. Week of Prayer for Christian Unity (18–25 January).
2027-01-18.verse: And no one puts new wine into old wineskins; otherwise, the wine will burst the skins, and the wine is lost, and so are the skins; but one puts new wine into fresh wineskins.”
theo: Hebrews begins its great teaching on Christ the High Priest. Every high priest is chosen from among mortals to offer gifts and sacrifices for sins, and “is able to deal gently with the ignorant and wayward, since he himself is subject to weakness.” Christ did not appoint himself; the Father said: “You are a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek.” And he learned his priesthood in suffering: “In the days of his flesh, Jesus offered up prayers and supplications, with loud cries and tears… Although he was a Son, he learned obedience through what he suffered.”

In the Gospel people ask why Jesus' disciples do not fast. He answers with images of joy and newness: wedding guests do not fast while the bridegroom is with them; no one sews new cloth on an old garment; “one puts new wine into fresh wineskins.” Christ brings something new that needs new hearts. Today the Week of Prayer for Christian Unity begins: divisions among Christians are old wineskins that cannot hold the new wine of Christ's love. We pray, as Jesus did, “that they may all be one.”
outline: Ask: what happens when new wine goes into old skins?
Christ's priestly prayer in his suffering.
Christ needs renewed hearts and a united Church.
live: Pray for unity (John 17:21)
Each day this week pray the Our Father for the unity of Christians.
Become a fresh wineskin
Let go of one old habit of thinking that resists Christ.
2027-01-18.prayer: Lord Jesus, High Priest who learned obedience through suffering, you pour new wine into our lives. Make our hearts new wineskins, and during this week of prayer make all Christians one, as you and the Father are one. Amen.
altar: At the altar Christ the eternal Priest offers himself. The cup of new wine is his Blood of the new covenant, which makes us one.

2027-01-19.title: Tuesday of the Second Week in Ordinary Time
readings: A sure and steadfast anchor of the soul
The Lord will remember his covenant for ever
The sabbath was made for humankind
2027-01-19.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 2 (Year I). Liturgical colour: green. Week of Prayer for Christian Unity (18–25 January).
2027-01-19.verse: We have this hope, a sure and steadfast anchor of the soul, a hope that enters the inner shrine behind the curtain,
theo: Hebrews encourages a tired community: “God is not unjust; he will not overlook your work and the love that you showed for his sake in serving the saints.” Do not become sluggish, but imitate those who “through faith and patience inherit the promises”, like Abraham. God bound himself by an oath, so that “we… might be strongly encouraged to seize the hope set before us. We have this hope, a sure and steadfast anchor of the soul.” Our anchor is not thrown into the shifting sand of this world; it is fixed in heaven, where Jesus has gone ahead of us.

In the Gospel the Pharisees object when the disciples pluck grain on the sabbath. Jesus recalls David eating the holy bread when he was hungry, and declares: “The sabbath was made for humankind, and not humankind for the sabbath; so the Son of Man is lord even of the sabbath.” God's laws are gifts for our life, not burdens to crush it. The Lord's Day is his gift of rest and worship, and Christ himself is its Lord.
outline: Ask: what keeps a ship steady in a storm?
Fixed in heaven where Jesus has gone.
“A sure and steadfast anchor of the soul.”
live: Keep going (Hebrews 6:11–12)
Return to one good work you have grown tired of.
Keep Sunday holy (Mark 2:27)
Plan this Sunday as a day of worship, family and rest.
2027-01-19.prayer: Faithful God, you never forget our love and you have given us hope as an anchor for the soul. Keep us patient in faith, and teach us to keep your day as a gift of life, with Christ the Lord of the sabbath. Amen.
altar: Hebrews says our hope enters “behind the curtain”, where Jesus our High Priest has gone. At Mass heaven's sanctuary touches earth.

2027-01-20.title: Wednesday of the Second Week in Ordinary Time · Sts Fabian and Sebastian
readings: A priest for ever, like Melchizedek
You are a priest for ever, in the line of Melchizedek
Is it lawful to do good on the sabbath?
2027-01-20.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 2 (Year I). Liturgical colour: green. Week of Prayer for Christian Unity (18–25 January). Optional memorials: St Fabian, pope and martyr; St Sebastian, martyr. In India St Sebastian is widely celebrated.
2027-01-20.verse: Then he said to them, “Is it lawful to do good or to do harm on the sabbath, to save life or to kill?” But they were silent.
theo: Hebrews reflects on the mysterious king Melchizedek, who “brought out bread and wine” and blessed Abraham. He appears in Scripture “without father, without mother, without genealogy”, and so “resembling the Son of God, he remains a priest forever.” Christ is a priest not by family descent like the Levites, but “through the power of an indestructible life”. The Church has always seen in Melchizedek's bread and wine a sign of the Eucharist.

In the synagogue a man with a withered hand stands before Jesus while his critics watch. Jesus asks: “Is it lawful to do good or to do harm on the sabbath, to save life or to kill?” They are silent. Mark says Jesus looked at them “with anger; he was grieved at their hardness of heart”, and healed the man. Hardness of heart grieves God more than any broken rule. Today many in Kerala honour St Sebastian, the soldier who served Christ before the emperor and gave his life rather than deny him, and St Fabian, pope and martyr. Both had hearts that were soft toward God and firm in the truth.
outline: Ask: what makes a heart hard?
Point 2 · Grieved at hardness of heart
“Is it lawful to do good… to save life?”
live: Soften your heart (Mark 3:5)
Ask God to show you one area where your heart has grown hard.
Courage like Sebastian
Defend someone who is treated unjustly at work or school.
2027-01-20.prayer: Lord Jesus, eternal priest like Melchizedek, you were grieved at hardness of heart. Soften my heart, give me courage like St Sebastian, and let me always choose to do good and to save life. Amen.
altar: Melchizedek offered bread and wine; Christ, priest for ever, offers his Body and Blood under these signs (Roman Canon).

2027-01-21.title: Saint Agnes, Virgin and Martyr
readings: He always lives to make intercession for them
Here am I, Lord; I come to do your will
Whenever the unclean spirits saw him, they shouted, You are the Son of God!
2027-01-21.alt: Memorial. Thursday of the Second Week in Ordinary Time (Year I). Week of Prayer for Christian Unity (18–25 January). Liturgical colour: red.
2027-01-21.verse: Consequently he is able for all time to save those who approach God through him, since he always lives to make intercession for them.
theo: Hebrews offers one of the most comforting truths in the New Testament: Christ “is able for all time to save those who approach God through him, since he always lives to make intercession for them.” Right now, at the Father's right hand, the risen Jesus is praying for you. Unlike earthly priests who offered sacrifices daily, he offered himself “once for all”, and is “the mediator of a better covenant”.

Mark describes crowds pressing on Jesus from every region, so many that he asks for a boat to be ready. “All who had diseases pressed upon him to touch him.” The unclean spirits fall before him and shout, “You are the Son of God!”, but he silences them; he will be revealed in his own way, on the Cross. Today we honour St Agnes, a Roman girl of about twelve or thirteen who refused to give up her consecration to Christ and was martyred around 304. The weakest in the world's eyes, she was strong because her Lord was interceding for her.
outline: Point 2 · Crowds press to touch him
Our need draws us to him.
A girl who conquered by faith.
“He always lives to make intercession for them.”
live: Rest in his prayer (Hebrews 7:25)
When anxious today, say: Jesus is praying for me now.
Protect the young
Pray for and support the protection of girls and children from exploitation.
2027-01-21.prayer: Lord Jesus, you live for ever to intercede for us. Draw us to touch you in faith, and through the prayers of St Agnes give us courage and purity to belong wholly to you. Amen.
altar: At every Mass Christ's eternal intercession is made present. We join his prayer to the Father.

2027-01-22.title: Friday of the Second Week in Ordinary Time
readings: I will put my laws in their minds and write them on their hearts
He appointed twelve to be with him and to be sent out
2027-01-22.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 2 (Year I). Liturgical colour: green. Week of Prayer for Christian Unity (18–25 January). Optional memorial: St Vincent, deacon and martyr.
2027-01-22.verse: And he appointed twelve, whom he also named apostles, to be with him, and to be sent out to proclaim the message, and to have authority to cast out demons.
theo: Hebrews quotes Jeremiah's great promise of a new covenant: “I will put my laws in their minds, and write them on their hearts, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people… For I will be merciful toward their iniquities, and I will remember their sins no more.” The old covenant was written on stone; the new is written by the Spirit on hearts. Christ is its mediator, and forgiveness is its foundation.

Mark shows Jesus forming the people of this new covenant. He goes up the mountain, as Moses did at Sinai, and “called to him those whom he wanted”. He appoints twelve, like the twelve tribes of Israel, for two purposes: “to be with him, and to be sent out”. First friendship, then mission. The list includes fishermen, a tax collector, a zealot and Judas who betrayed him: Jesus calls ordinary, mixed and imperfect people. Every Christian vocation has the same two movements: being with Jesus in prayer, and being sent by him to others.
outline: Ask: why did Jesus choose twelve?
Point 1 · A new covenant on hearts
“To be with him, and to be sent out.”
live: Be with him (Mark 3:14)
Give fifteen quiet minutes to Jesus today.
Be sent
Do one act of witness or service in his name today.
2027-01-22.prayer: Lord Jesus, mediator of the new covenant, you called the Twelve to be with you and to be sent out. Write your law on my heart, keep me close to you, and send me to bring your mercy to others. Amen.
altar: At the altar we hear the words: “the new and eternal covenant.” Then the Mass ends: “Go forth.” With him, then sent.

2027-01-23.title: Saturday of the Second Week in Ordinary Time
readings: The blood of Christ will purify our conscience
God mounts his throne amid shouts of joy
His family said: He has gone out of his mind
2027-01-23.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 2 (Year I). Liturgical colour: green. Week of Prayer for Christian Unity (18–25 January). Optional: Saturday memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary; St Marianne Cope (USA).
2027-01-23.verse: how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without blemish to God, purify our conscience from dead works to worship the living God!
theo: Hebrews describes the old tabernacle with its Holy Place and its Holy of Holies, where the high priest entered once a year with the blood of animals. Then it announces the fulfilment: “when Christ came as a high priest of the good things that have come… he entered once for all into the Holy Place, not with the blood of goats and calves, but with his own blood, thus obtaining eternal redemption.” If animal blood could purify the flesh, “how much more will the blood of Christ… purify our conscience from dead works to worship the living God!”

Mark's Gospel today has only two verses. Jesus comes home, and the crowd is so great that “they could not even eat.” His relatives go out to restrain him, “for people were saying, ‘He has gone out of his mind.’” Total self-giving looks like madness to the world. The One who offered himself without blemish to God seemed foolish even to his own family. Love that gives everything always appears a little mad. On this Saturday we remember Mary, who stood by her Son when others did not understand.
outline: Ask: has anyone ever thought you were foolish for doing good?
Christ enters with his own blood.
From dead works to living worship.
His family thought he was out of his mind.
“The blood of Christ… purify our conscience.”
live: Examine your conscience (Hebrews 9:14)
Make an examination of conscience tonight and plan confession.
Love generously
Do one generous act that others may think excessive.
2027-01-23.prayer: Lord Jesus, you entered the sanctuary with your own blood and obtained eternal redemption. Purify my conscience from dead works, give me the holy madness of your love, and keep me near your Mother, who understood you when others did not. Amen.
altar: The chalice holds the Blood of Christ that purifies our conscience. At Mass we worship the living God with hearts made clean.

2027-01-25.title: The Conversion of Saint Paul, Apostle
readings: Get up, be baptized, and have your sins washed away
Go out to all the world and tell the good news
Go into all the world and proclaim the good news
2027-01-25.alt: Feast. Gloria is said. Conclusion of the Week of Prayer for Christian Unity. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-01-25.verse: I asked, ‘What am I to do, Lord?’ The Lord said to me, ‘Get up and go to Damascus; there you will be told everything that has been assigned to you to do.’
theo: The Church celebrates no other conversion with a feast of its own; Paul's is unique because it shows what grace can do with the fiercest enemy. Paul tells the story himself, standing before a hostile crowd in Jerusalem: “I persecuted this Way up to the point of death.” On the road to Damascus, at noon, “a great light from heaven suddenly shone about me. I fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to me, ‘Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me?’” He asks: “Who are you, Lord?” And the answer reveals everything: “I am Jesus of Nazareth whom you are persecuting.”

Jesus does not say “my followers” but “me”. Whoever touches the Church touches Christ, for the Church is his Body. Blinded, Paul is led by the hand into Damascus. There Ananias, a devout disciple, comes to him: “Brother Saul, regain your sight!” and tells him: “you will be his witness to all the world of what you have seen and heard. And now why do you delay? Get up, be baptized, and have your sins washed away, calling on his name.” Conversion is not complete without the Church: Paul needs Ananias, Baptism and the community he once persecuted.

The Gospel gives the risen Lord's command: “Go into all the world and proclaim the good news to the whole creation.” Paul became the great missionary of that command. The Week of Prayer for Christian Unity ends today, because Paul, who once divided by violence, became the apostle who wrote: “There is one body and one Spirit… one Lord, one faith, one baptism.” No one is beyond conversion, and no division is beyond healing.
conn: Three accounts.
Luke tells the conversion three times in Acts (9, 22, 26), a sign of its importance.
Saul, Saul.
The double name recalls God's calls to Abraham, Jacob, Moses and Samuel at turning points of salvation history.
“Me”.
St Augustine: Christ, the Head in heaven, cries out for his Body on earth.
Ananias.
A disciple who was afraid of Saul yet obeyed (Acts 9:13–17); every conversion needs an Ananias.
Unity Week.
The Week of Prayer for Christian Unity (18–25 January) ends on this feast.
The Apostle to the Nations.
Paul made at least three great missionary journeys and thirteen letters in the New Testament bear his name; he was martyred in Rome under Nero.
altar: At the altar we receive the Body of the One who said “Saul, why are you persecuting me?” The Eucharist makes us his Body.
Like Paul, we are sent from the altar: “Go forth, the Mass is ended.”
outline: Ask: who is the most unlikely person you can imagine becoming a saint?
Point 4 · Go into all the world
live: Ask Paul's question
Pray each morning this week: What am I to do, Lord?
Be an Ananias
Reach out to someone who has wronged the Church or you.
Pray for unity
End the Unity Week by praying for one Christian community other than your own.
Share the good news
Tell one person how God has changed your life.
fathers: St John Chrysostom (in substance)
Paul's soul was a meadow of virtues; the persecutor became the trumpet of Christ.
St Augustine (in substance)
Saul was struck down to be raised up; the wolf became a shepherd.
magis: The Church as the Body of Christ.
There can be no ecumenism without interior conversion.
Paul's encounter with the risen Christ; the Church, Body of Christ.
The second conversion of the baptized.
saints: Born in Tarsus, a Pharisee, converted about AD 34–36, apostle to the nations, martyred in Rome under Nero.
2027-01-25.prayer: O God, who taught the whole world through the preaching of the blessed Apostle Paul, draw us, we pray, nearer to you through the example of him whose conversion we celebrate today, and so make us witnesses to your truth in the world. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen.

2027-01-26.title: Saints Timothy and Titus, Bishops
readings: Rekindle the gift of God that is within you
Proclaim his marvellous deeds to all the nations
Whoever does the will of God is my brother and sister and mother
2027-01-26.alt: Memorial. In India, Republic Day: the Mass for the Nation may be used where the bishops permit. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-01-26.verse: for this reason I remind you to rekindle the gift of God that is within you through the laying on of my hands;
theo: The day after Paul's conversion, the Church honours two of his closest companions, Timothy and Titus. Paul writes to Timothy with fatherly warmth: “I am reminded of your sincere faith, a faith that lived first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice.” And he gives him a charge: “rekindle the gift of God that is within you… for God did not give us a spirit of cowardice, but rather a spirit of power and of love and of self-discipline.” Grace received at ordination, or at Baptism and Confirmation, can grow cold; it must be fanned into flame.

In the Gospel his mother and brothers come and, standing outside, ask for him; Jesus looks at those sitting around him: “Here are my mother and my brothers! Whoever does the will of God is my brother and sister and mother.” This does not reject Mary, who more than anyone did God's will; it opens his family to all who obey. Today India celebrates Republic Day. As citizens and as members of God's family, we pray for our country, for justice and harmony among all its peoples, and for those who govern.
outline: Ask: is there a gift of God in you that has grown cold?
Doing the will of God; praying for our nation.
“Rekindle the gift of God that is within you.”
live: Rekindle a gift (2 Timothy 1:6)
Use one gift you have neglected: music, teaching, prayer, service.
Pray for India
Pray for the nation and its leaders on Republic Day.
2027-01-26.prayer: O God, who adorned Saints Timothy and Titus with apostolic virtues, grant, through the intercession of them both, that, living justly and devoutly in this present age, we may merit to reach our heavenly homeland. Bless our nation on this Republic Day with justice, peace and harmony. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: The laying on of hands that made Timothy a bishop continues in the Church today; through it Christ gives us the Eucharist.

2027-01-27.title: Wednesday of the Third Week in Ordinary Time
readings: By a single offering he has perfected for all time those who are sanctified
You are a priest for ever, in the line of Melchizedek
A sower went out to sow
2027-01-27.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 3 (Year I). Liturgical colour: green. Optional memorial of St Angela Merici, virgin (white).
2027-01-27.verse: And these are the ones sown on the good soil: they hear the word and accept it and bear fruit, thirty and sixty and a hundredfold.”
theo: Hebrews contrasts the priests of the old covenant, who stand “day after day… offering again and again the same sacrifices that can never take away sins”, with Christ, who “offered for all time a single sacrifice for sins” and then “sat down at the right hand of God”. The priest who sits has finished his work. “By a single offering he has perfected for all time those who are sanctified.” And God's promise through Jeremiah is fulfilled: “I will remember their sins and their lawless deeds no more.” The Mass does not repeat this sacrifice; it makes the one sacrifice present.

In the Gospel Jesus teaches from a boat, and the first great parable is the sower. Seed falls on the path, on rock, among thorns and on good soil. Jesus explains: Satan takes the word away; trouble makes the shallow fall away; “the cares of the world, and the lure of wealth, and the desire for other things come in and choke the word”. But those on good soil “hear the word and accept it and bear fruit”. St Angela Merici, founder of the Ursulines, gave her life to teaching girls the faith, sowing the word in young hearts. Our task is to be good soil and good sowers.
outline: Ask: what crowds out God's word in your day?
Point 1 · The priest who sat down
“They hear the word and accept it and bear fruit.”
live: Pull a thorn (Mark 4:19)
Identify one worry or desire that chokes God's word, and cut it back.
Sow the word
Share a verse of Scripture with a young person, as St Angela did.
