2027-01-27.prayer: Lord Jesus, by your single offering you have perfected those who are sanctified. Make our hearts good soil for your word, free from the thorns of worry and wealth, and through the prayers of St Angela Merici make us sowers of your word for the young. Amen.
altar: At Mass the one sacrifice of Christ is made present; we do not add to it, we enter into it.

2027-01-28.title: Saint Thomas Aquinas, Priest and Doctor of the Church
readings: Let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith
Such are the people who seek your face, O Lord
Is a lamp brought in to be put under the bushel basket?
2027-01-28.verse: He said to them, “Is a lamp brought in to be put under the bushel basket, or under the bed, and not on the lampstand?
theo: Hebrews tells us that we have “confidence to enter the sanctuary by the blood of Jesus, by the new and living way that he opened for us through the curtain (that is, through his flesh)”. So: “let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith… Let us hold fast to the confession of our hope without wavering… And let us consider how to provoke one another to love and good deeds, not neglecting to meet together.” Faith, hope and love, lived in community, especially in the Sunday assembly.

Jesus asks: “Is a lamp brought in to be put under the bushel basket?” The light of the Gospel is meant to shine. Few have let it shine more brightly than St Thomas Aquinas, the Dominican friar whose mind served the faith with clarity and humility. He taught that faith and reason are two lights from the one God. Near the end of his life, after an experience at Mass, he stopped writing, saying that all he had written seemed like straw compared with what he had seen. He wrote the hymns we sing before the Blessed Sacrament: Pange lingua, Tantum ergo, Adoro te devote. His learning ended in adoration.
outline: Ask: do you think faith and reason are enemies or friends?
Point 2 · Do not neglect to meet
Point 3 · The lamp on the stand
“Is a lamp… put under the bushel basket?”
live: Study the faith
Read one paragraph of the Catechism today and think about it.
Adore
Spend ten minutes before the Blessed Sacrament, praying Adoro te devote.
2027-01-28.prayer: O God, who made Saint Thomas Aquinas outstanding in his zeal for holiness and his study of sacred doctrine, grant us, we pray, that we may understand what he taught and imitate what he accomplished. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen.
altar: St Thomas taught that in the Eucharist Christ is present whole and entire, by the change the Church calls transubstantiation. His hymns still lead us to adore.

2027-01-29.title: Friday of the Third Week in Ordinary Time
readings: Do not abandon that confidence of yours
The salvation of the righteous is from the Lord
The seed grows, he does not know how; the mustard seed
2027-01-29.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 3 (Year I). Liturgical colour: green.
2027-01-29.verse: He also said, “The kingdom of God is as if someone would scatter seed on the ground, and would sleep and rise night and day, and the seed would sprout and grow, he does not know how.
theo: Hebrews reminds a tired community of its early courage: “Recall those earlier days when, after you had been enlightened, you endured a hard struggle with sufferings… you cheerfully accepted the plundering of your possessions.” Now they are tempted to give up. “Do not, therefore, abandon that confidence of yours; it brings a great reward. For you need endurance.” Faith is not only a beginning; it is a long faithfulness. “We are not among those who shrink back and so are lost, but among those who have faith and so are saved.”

Jesus gives two small parables that are a medicine for discouragement. A farmer scatters seed, sleeps and rises, “and the seed would sprout and grow, he does not know how.” The earth produces “first the stalk, then the head, then the full grain in the head.” And the mustard seed, “the smallest of all the seeds on earth”, becomes a shrub where the birds nest. God's Kingdom grows quietly, slowly and surely, often while we sleep. Our part is to sow faithfully and to trust; the growth belongs to God.
outline: Ask: have you ever planted something and waited impatiently?
Point 2 · The seed grows by itself
“The seed would sprout and grow, he does not know how.”
live: Endure (Hebrews 10:36)
Keep going with one good thing you are tempted to give up.
Sow small
Do one small act of faith today and leave the results to God.
2027-01-29.prayer: Lord God, your Kingdom grows like seed in the night and like the smallest of seeds. Give us endurance not to shrink back, patience to sow and wait, and trust that you give the growth. Amen.
altar: A small piece of bread becomes the Body of Christ; the smallest seeds of God's Kingdom are planted in us at every Communion.

2027-01-30.title: Saturday of the Third Week in Ordinary Time
readings: He looked forward to the city that has foundations, whose architect and builder is God
Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel; he has come to his people
Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?
2027-01-30.alt: Weekday of Ordinary Time, Week 3 (Year I). Liturgical colour: green. Saturday memorial of the Blessed Virgin Mary may be celebrated (white).
2027-01-30.verse: Now faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen.
theo: Hebrews 11 is the great chapter of faith: “Now faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen.” Abraham “set out, not knowing where he was going.” He lived in tents in the promised land, “for he looked forward to the city that has foundations, whose architect and builder is God.” Sarah, past the age, “considered him faithful who had promised.” And when tested, Abraham offered Isaac, reasoning “that God is able even to raise someone from the dead”. Faith is not certainty about the road; it is trust in the One who calls.

In the Gospel the disciples cross the lake at evening. A great windstorm arises; the boat is filling with water; and Jesus is asleep on the cushion in the stern. “Teacher, do you not care that we are perishing?” He rises, rebukes the wind, says to the sea, “Peace! Be still!”, and there is a dead calm. Then he asks: “Why are you afraid? Have you still no faith?” They are filled with awe: “Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?” Jesus asleep in the storm is not indifferent; he is the Lord of creation, and his presence in the boat is enough. With Mary, who believed without seeing, we learn to trust.
outline: Ask: when has life felt like a boat in a storm?
Not knowing where he was going.
“Why are you afraid? Have you still no faith?”
live: Trust in the storm (Mark 4:40)
Name your current storm and hand it to Jesus in prayer.
Walk by faith
Take one step God is asking of you without knowing the whole road.
2027-01-30.prayer: Lord Jesus, you calmed the wind and the sea with a word. In the storms of our lives, give us the faith of Abraham, who set out not knowing where he was going, and the trust of Mary, who believed your word. Peace! Be still! Amen.
altar: At every Mass the Lord who calmed the storm is with us in the boat of the Church, and says: peace be with you.

quick: Mary is truly the Mother of God, because her Son is God.
God sent his Son so that we may become his children.
The new year begins with the blessing of the Lord and the name of Jesus.
2027-01-01.action: Bless each member of your family with the words of Numbers 6:24–26.
2027-01-01.question: What will I ponder in my heart this year, as Mary did?
catechism: Mary is truly Mother of God.
kidsaint: She held Jesus in her arms and kept all his words in her heart. Lesson: we can talk to Jesus quietly in our heart every day.
2027-01-01.special: Solemnity of Mary, the Holy Mother of God. Octave Day of Christmas. World Day of Peace. Colour: white.
term: Greek for “God-bearer”: Mary bore the eternal Son in his human nature, so she is truly Mother of God (CCC 495).

family.explain: The shepherds found baby Jesus with Mary and Joseph. Mary kept everything in her heart and thought about it. On the eighth day the baby was named Jesus.
family.intention: We pray for peace in the world and in our home this year.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing God did for our family last year?”

illus: An illustration

A grandmother in Thrissur kept a small diary for fifty years. Each night she wrote one line: what God had done that day. When she died, her grandchildren read it and found a whole family history of grace: births, illnesses healed, quarrels mended. She had pondered, like Mary, and her family discovered how faithful God had been.

pm.open: Holy Mary, Mother of God, you kept the words of your Son in your heart. On this first day of the year we gather with you around Jesus. Lord, bless us and keep us, and give us your peace. Amen.
share: “The LORD bless you and keep you” (Numbers 6:24). Which blessing of last year am I most grateful for?
Mary pondered all these things (Luke 2:19). How can I make silence for God this year?
God sent his Son so that we might be his children (Galatians 4:4–7). What does it mean to me to call God Abba?
pm.resp: Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us.
interc: For the Church, that like Mary she may bring Christ to the world.
For peace among nations, and for an end to war and violence.
For our families, that the Lord may bless and keep them all through this year.
For mothers, especially those who are expecting a child or who grieve a child.
For our group, that we may ponder the Word each day.
pm.close: Lord God, you gave us your Son through the Virgin Mary. Through her prayers bless this new year, keep us in your love and give us your peace. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Christ is revealed to all the nations.
The Magi seek with the star and find with the Scriptures.
Whoever adores Christ goes home by another road.
2027-01-03.action: Offer Christ one concrete gift this week.
2027-01-03.question: What is the star God is using to lead me to Christ, and am I following it?
kidsaint: Wise men who travelled very far following a star to find baby Jesus, and gave him their best gifts. Lesson: give Jesus your best, not your leftovers.
2027-01-03.special: Solemnity of the Epiphany of the Lord. Proclamation of the date of Easter 2027 (28 March). Colour: white.
term: Greek for “manifestation”: Christ is shown as Saviour of all nations in the Magi, at the Jordan and at Cana (CCC 528).

family.explain: Wise men from far away saw a special star. They followed it to Bethlehem, found baby Jesus with Mary, knelt down and gave him gold, frankincense and myrrh.
family.intention: We pray for people in every country who do not yet know Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “What gift can each of us give Jesus this week?”

illus: An illustration

A young engineer from Chennai, working abroad, began reading the Gospels only out of curiosity about the churches he saw. One verse led to another, a parish priest answered his questions, and two years later he was baptised at the Easter Vigil. He said: I was not looking for a religion, I was following a light, and it stopped over a Person.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, light of the nations, you drew the Magi from the East by a star. Draw us too, and receive the gifts of our hearts. Amen.
share: Isaiah says, “Arise, shine; for your light has come” (Isaiah 60:1). Where has Christ's light come into my life?
The Magi searched; the scribes stayed home (Matthew 2:4–6). Am I a seeker or a spectator?
They went home by another road (Matthew 2:12). What must change after I meet Christ?
pm.resp: Lord, every nation on earth will adore you.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a light to every nation.
For missionaries, especially in India and Asia.
For those who search for God sincerely, that they may find Christ.
For rulers who feel threatened by the truth, like Herod, that they may be converted.
For our group, that we may offer Christ our gold, frankincense and myrrh.
pm.close: Lord God, you led the Magi by a star to your Son. Lead us by faith to see your glory, and send us home by another road, changed by your love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jesus prays on the mountain and sees us straining.
He comes across the storm: it is I, do not be afraid.
Perfect love casts out fear.
2027-01-06.action: Tell Jesus the one fear that troubles you most this year.
2027-01-06.question: Do I trust that Jesus sees me when I am straining at the oars?

family.explain: The disciples were in a boat in a strong wind at night. Jesus came walking on the water and said: do not be afraid, it is me! He got into the boat and the wind stopped.
family.intention: We pray for fishermen and all who travel by sea.
family.ask: Ask: “When do you feel afraid? Let us tell Jesus about it.”

illus: An illustration

A fisherman from Vizhinjam was caught by a cyclone far from shore. For two nights he and his companions tied themselves to their boat. He said afterwards: I kept saying one line I learned as a child, Jesus, I trust in you. The wind did not stop at once, but the fear did.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you come to us in every storm and say: Take heart, it is I. Calm our hearts as we gather, and fill us with your love. Amen.
share: Jesus went up the mountain to pray (Mark 6:46). Do I believe that he prays for me?
Take heart, it is I (Mark 6:50). In what storm do I need to hear these words?
Perfect love casts out fear (1 John 4:18). How can love overcome a fear in my life?
interc: For the Church in times of persecution, that she may not be afraid.
For fishermen, sailors and all who travel.
For those who live in fear: of illness, of debt, of violence.
For families going through storms.
For our group, that our love may drive out fear.
pm.close: Lord God, your Son came to his disciples across the stormy sea. Come to us in our fears, and let your perfect love make us brave. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: At the Jordan the heavens open and the Trinity is revealed.
Jesus is anointed with the Spirit for doing good.
In Baptism the Father calls each of us his beloved child.
2027-01-10.action: Find out your baptismal date and write it down.
2027-01-10.question: Do I live as one whom the Father calls beloved?
kidsaint: He baptised Jesus and pointed everyone to him. Lesson: help others to come close to Jesus.
2027-01-10.special: Feast of the Baptism of the Lord. End of the Christmas season. Colour: white.
term: Greek for “calling down”: the prayer asking the Father to send the Holy Spirit, at Baptism on the water and at Mass on the bread and wine (CCC 1105–1106).

family.explain: Jesus was baptised in the river Jordan. The sky opened, the Holy Spirit came like a dove, and God the Father said: you are my Son, I love you!
family.intention: We pray for babies who will be baptised this year and for their godparents.
family.ask: Ask: “Let us look at photos of our Baptisms. Who are our godparents?”

illus: An illustration

A parish in Kollam started a simple custom: every child receives a card with the date of their Baptism, and on that day the family lights the baptismal candle at supper. A teacher said her pupils now know their baptism days as well as their birthdays, and some insist on going to Mass that day.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, at the Jordan the heavens opened and the Father called you his beloved Son. Open heaven over us as we gather, and renew in us the grace of our Baptism. Amen.
share: “Here is my servant… I have put my spirit upon him” (Isaiah 42:1). How does the Spirit work in me?
“God anointed Jesus… he went about doing good” (Acts 10:38). What good can I do this week?
“You are my Son, the Beloved” (Mark 1:11). Do I believe God says this to me?
pm.resp: Lord, renew in us the grace of Baptism.
interc: For all the baptised, that they may live as children of God.
For catechumens preparing for Baptism at Easter.
For parents and godparents, that they may hand on the faith.
For those who have drifted from the faith received in Baptism.
For our group, that we may go about doing good like Jesus.
pm.close: Father, at the Jordan you anointed your Son with the Spirit. Keep us faithful to our Baptism, and send us out to do good in his name. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jesus asks: what are you looking for?
He invites: come and see; and they stay with him.
Andrew brings his brother: faith spreads person to person.
2027-01-17.action: Invite one person to Mass or a prayer group this week.
2027-01-17.question: What am I really looking for, and have I brought it to Jesus?
catechism: Purity of heart and the body as temple.
kidsaint: When he met Jesus, the first thing he did was bring his brother Peter. Lesson: when you love Jesus, share him with your family and friends.
2027-01-17.special: Second Sunday in Ordinary Time, Year B. Week of Prayer for Christian Unity begins tomorrow.
term: From the Latin for “calling”: God's personal call to each person, to life, faith, holiness and a particular way of serving (CCC 1877, 2013).

family.explain: Two friends of John the Baptist followed Jesus. Jesus asked: what are you looking for? He said: come and see! They stayed with him all afternoon. Then Andrew ran to bring his brother Peter.
family.intention: We pray for young people, that they may hear God's call.
family.ask: Ask: “Who brought you to know Jesus? Whom can we bring?”

illus: An illustration

A young man from Thrissur working in Dubai had stopped going to church. A colleague simply said one Friday: come with me to Mass; just come and see. He went, stayed for the coffee afterwards, and kept coming. Five years later he leads the parish youth group. He says: nobody argued with me; someone just invited me.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you asked your first disciples: what are you looking for? Here we are, looking for you. Let us come and see, and stay with you. Amen.
share: “Speak, for your servant is listening” (1 Samuel 3:10). How do I listen for God's voice?
“What are you looking for?” (John 1:38). What do I really seek?
“We have found the Messiah” (John 1:41). Whom can I bring to Jesus?
pm.resp: Here I am, Lord; I come to do your will.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a home where people come and see Jesus.
For vocations to the priesthood and religious life.
For parents, teachers and priests who, like Eli, guide young people.
For those searching for meaning, that they may meet Christ.
For our group, that we may be Andrews who bring others.
pm.close: Father, your Son invites us to come and see. Make us disciples who stay with him and bring others to him. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The time is fulfilled; the Kingdom has come near.
Repent and believe in the good news.
The fishermen left their nets immediately and followed Jesus.
2027-01-24.action: Place the Bible in a place of honour at home and begin reading Mark.
2027-01-24.question: What net must I leave to follow Jesus?
catechism: Christ, the one Word of Scripture.
Scripture in the life of the Church; ignorance of Scripture is ignorance of Christ.
kidsaint: A fisherman who left his nets when Jesus called, then brought his brother Peter to Jesus. Lesson: when you meet Jesus, bring your friends to him too!
2027-01-24.special: Sunday of the Word of God. Week of Prayer for Christian Unity.
term: Prayerful reading of Scripture in four steps: reading, meditation, prayer, contemplation.

family.explain: Jesus saw two brothers fishing and said: come, follow me! They put down their nets right away and went with him.
family.intention: We pray that our family may love God's word.
family.ask: Ask: “Where shall we keep our family Bible so that we read it every day?”

illus: An illustration

In a fishing village near Kollam, a parish began a custom on the Sunday of the Word of God: every family carries its Bible in procession to the altar for a blessing and takes it home to a place of honour. An old fisherman said: Jesus called fishermen first; it is right that fishermen should carry his word.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, your word is near us. As on the shore of Galilee, call us again and give us the courage to follow. Amen.
share: The time is fulfilled (Mark 1:15). Do I live as if God's moment is now?
Immediately they left their nets (Mark 1:18). What holds me back?
The present form of this world is passing away (1 Corinthians 7:31). What do I cling to as if it were final?
pm.resp: Lord, make us know your ways.
interc: For the Church, that she may love and proclaim God's word.
For Bible translators, teachers and catechists.
For those called to leave everything and follow Christ.
For the unity of all Christians.
For our group, that we may read Scripture daily.
pm.close: God our Father, your Son called the first disciples by the sea. Through your word, call us and keep us faithful. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God promised a prophet like Moses; Jesus is that prophet.
Jesus teaches with authority and commands unclean spirits.
Today, listen to his voice; do not harden your hearts.
2027-01-31.action: Spend five minutes in silence with today's Gospel.
2027-01-31.question: What in me needs to hear Jesus say: be silent, and come out?
catechism: The signs of the Kingdom; victory over Satan.
Virginity for the Kingdom and marriage.
kidsaint: A priest in Italy who loved poor street boys. He taught them, played games with them and showed them Jesus. Lesson: we can help other children know Jesus through kindness and fun!
2027-01-31.special: Fourth Sunday in Ordinary Time. St John Bosco not kept this year.
term: Greek for authority: the power that comes from who one is. Jesus teaches with exousia, not by quoting others.

family.explain: Jesus taught in the synagogue and everyone was amazed. A man with a bad spirit shouted, and Jesus said: be quiet, come out! And the man was free.
family.intention: We pray for all young people, through St John Bosco.
family.ask: Ask: “What does Jesus want us to listen to today?”

illus: An illustration

A Salesian priest in Kochi runs a centre for boys who once lived at the railway station. One boy, addicted to glue, said after a year: on the street every voice told me what I was worth. At the centre I heard one voice that said I was God's son. That voice had authority. It set me free.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Holy One of God, speak to us with authority, and free us from all that binds us. Amen.
share: I will put my words in the mouth of the prophet (Deuteronomy 18:18). Do I hear Jesus as God's own voice?
He taught them as one having authority (Mark 1:22). Whose authority rules my choices?
O that today you would listen (Psalm 95:7). Where am I hardening my heart?
interc: For the Church, that she may proclaim Christ's word with courage.
For those bound by addiction or evil.
For young people at risk, through St John Bosco.
For priests and consecrated men and women.
For our group, that we may not harden our hearts.
pm.close: God our Father, your Son speaks with authority and sets us free. Open our ears and soften our hearts. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: John the Baptist is a voice that points to Christ.
Remain in the faith you received from the beginning.
Basil and Gregory, holy friends, defended faith in the Trinity.
2027-01-02.action: In one conversation today, point to Christ rather than to yourself.
2027-01-02.question: Does my life point to Christ or to myself?

family.explain: People asked John the Baptist if he was the Messiah. He said no: I am only a voice. Jesus is the one who is coming.
family.intention: We pray for our friends, that we may help each other to be good.
family.ask: Ask: “Who is a friend that helps me to love Jesus?”

illus: An illustration

A sign at a railway crossing in Kerala reads only “Stop, look, go.” Nobody admires the sign; everyone obeys it and looks at the train. John the Baptist was content to be such a sign: people looked past him and saw Jesus.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, John the Baptist was the voice and you are the Word. Help us to point to you in all we say and do. Amen.
share: John said, “I am the voice” (John 1:23). How can my words make way for Jesus?
Let what you heard from the beginning abide in you (1 John 2:24). Who first taught me the faith?
Basil and Gregory were friends in God. Who is a friend who helps my faith?
interc: For bishops and teachers of the faith, that they may hand on the truth with love.
For theologians, that like Basil and Gregory they may serve the Church.
For friendships, that they may lead people to God.
For those who have abandoned the faith, that what they heard from the beginning may return to them.
For our group, that we may be voices for Christ.
pm.close: Lord God, you raised up Saints Basil and Gregory to defend the truth. Keep us faithful to the faith we received, and make us humble witnesses of your Son. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jesus begins his preaching where people sit in darkness.
His first word is: repent.
Test every spirit by Christ who came in the flesh.
2027-01-04.action: Name one habit that turns you away from God and take one step back today.
2027-01-04.question: Where in my life am I still sitting in darkness?

family.explain: Jesus went to live in Capernaum by the lake. People there were sad and in darkness, but Jesus came like a great light. He said: turn back to God!
family.intention: We pray for people who feel sad or lost.
family.ask: Ask: “What can we do to bring a little light to someone this week?”

illus: An illustration

During a power cut in a hostel in Kottayam, the students sat in complete darkness. One boy lit a single candle and placed it in the corridor. Within minutes everyone had gathered around it, and someone began a song. One small light changed the whole evening. Jesus came to Galilee as such a light.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are the great light that dawned on those who sat in darkness. Shine on us as we gather, and turn our hearts to you. Amen.
share: The people who sat in darkness have seen a great light (Matthew 4:16). Where has Christ brought light to me?
Jesus' first word is “Repent” (Matthew 4:17). What do I need to turn away from?
Test the spirits (1 John 4:1). How do I know which voices to follow?
interc: For those who preach the Gospel, that they may call people to conversion with love.
For regions where Christ is not known.
For the sick, that Christ may heal them as in Galilee.
For those confused by false teachings.
For our group, that we may grow in true conversion.
pm.close: Lord God, your Son brought light to Galilee of the Gentiles. Let his light shine in us and through us, and keep us faithful to his Spirit. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God is love, and he loved us first.
Jesus has compassion on the crowd like a shepherd.
He multiplies our little when we give it to him.
2027-01-05.action: Give a meal or groceries to a family in need this week.
2027-01-05.question: What are my five loaves that Jesus is asking me to give?

family.explain: Many hungry people followed Jesus. A few loaves and fish were all they had. Jesus blessed them, and everyone ate until they were full!
family.intention: We pray for children who go to bed hungry.
family.ask: Ask: “What can our family share with someone this week?”

illus: An illustration

In a parish in Palakkad, a widow began cooking one extra packet of rice each day for a sick neighbour. Others heard and joined her. A year later the parish kitchen was feeding forty people daily. It began with one packet given with love.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you had compassion on the crowd and fed them with your word and with bread. Feed us now, and make us generous. Amen.
share: God is love (1 John 4:8). How have I experienced God's love this week?
He had compassion for them (Mark 6:34). Whom do I find it hard to have compassion for?
You give them something to eat (Mark 6:37). What can I give?
interc: For the Church, that she may show the compassion of the Good Shepherd.
For the hungry and the poor of our land.
For farmers and all who produce our food.
For those who feel like sheep without a shepherd.
For our group, that we may share what we have.
pm.close: Lord God, you are love, and you loved us first. Make us share our bread and our lives, as your Son shared himself with us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jesus is the Anointed One, sent to the poor and the captive.
God's word is fulfilled today.
We cannot love God and hate our brother.
2027-01-07.action: Make peace with a family member you have been cold towards.
2027-01-07.question: Is God's word fulfilled “today” in my life, or only remembered?

family.explain: In his home town Jesus read from the Bible in the synagogue. He said: God's Spirit sent me to help the poor and free those who are in prison. Today it is happening!
family.intention: We pray for prisoners and their families.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we bring good news to someone poor or sad this week?”

illus: An illustration

A prison chaplain in Kannur reads Luke 4 with inmates every Christmas season. One year a man serving a life sentence said: if Jesus came for captives, then he came for me. He began studying, became a teacher for other prisoners, and now leads their Sunday prayer.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, the Spirit of the Lord is upon you. Speak your word to us today, and let it be fulfilled in our lives. Amen.
share: The Spirit of the Lord is upon me (Luke 4:18). Where do I see the Spirit at work today?
Today this scripture has been fulfilled (Luke 4:21). What word of God do I need to let come true in me?
We love because he first loved us (1 John 4:19). Whom do I find hard to love?
pm.resp: Lord, let your word be fulfilled today.
interc: For the poor, that they may hear good news through the Church.
For prisoners and captives, that they may find freedom in Christ.
For the blind and the sick.
For confessors and canon lawyers, through the prayers of St Raymond.
For our group, that our love for God may be seen in love for one another.
pm.close: Lord God, you anointed your Son with the Holy Spirit to bring good news to the poor. Let his word be fulfilled today in us, and make our love for you visible in love for our neighbour. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The leper trusts Jesus' power and asks for his will.
Jesus touches the untouchable and makes him clean.
Whoever has the Son has life.
2027-01-08.action: Bring to confession the sin you are most ashamed of.
2027-01-08.question: What part of my life am I afraid to let Jesus touch?

family.explain: A man had a terrible skin disease, and nobody would touch him. He asked Jesus for help. Jesus touched him and he was healed!
family.intention: We pray for people with leprosy and other diseases that make others stay away.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone at school or in our street that others leave alone? How can we be kind to them?”

illus: An illustration

St Damien of Molokai went to live among people with leprosy in Hawaii. He dressed their wounds, built their homes and celebrated Mass for them. One Sunday he began his homily with the words “We lepers”: he had caught the disease. He had touched them as Jesus did, all the way.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you stretched out your hand and touched the leper. Touch us now, heal what is broken in us, and make us your hands for others. Amen.
share: “Lord, if you choose, you can make me clean” (Luke 5:12). What do I want to ask Jesus to heal?
Jesus touched him (Luke 5:13). Whom do I avoid touching or meeting?
Whoever has the Son has life (1 John 5:12). How do I experience this life?
pm.resp: Lord, touch us and heal us.
interc: For people with leprosy, HIV and other diseases that bring rejection.
For doctors, nurses and all who care for the sick.
For those who feel unclean because of their sins, that they may come to confession.
For the Church, that she may touch the untouchable with Christ's love.
For our group, that we may pray as Jesus prayed in deserted places.
pm.close: Lord God, your Son stretched out his hand to heal the leper. Let his hand rest on us in the sacraments, and make us instruments of his healing. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jesus is the Bridegroom; John is his friend.
He must increase; I must decrease.
Keep yourselves from idols.
2027-01-09.action: Praise sincerely someone whose success you envy.
2027-01-09.question: Where do I want to increase instead of letting Christ increase?

family.explain: John the Baptist's friends were sad because people were going to Jesus. John said: I am happy! Jesus must become greater, and I must become smaller.
family.intention: We pray that we may be happy when others do well.
family.ask: Ask: “When were you happy because something good happened to someone else?”

illus: An illustration

At a wedding in Kottayam, the best man spent the whole day running errands, settling guests and making sure the groom was at ease. At the end someone thanked him, and he said: today is not my day; my joy is to see my friend happy. That is John the Baptist's joy.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are the Bridegroom, and we rejoice to hear your voice. Increase in us as we gather, and let our pride decrease. Amen.
share: He must increase, but I must decrease (John 3:30). Where do I need to become smaller?
The friend of the bridegroom rejoices (John 3:29). Can I rejoice in others' success?
Little children, keep yourselves from idols (1 John 5:21). What idol competes with God in my heart?
interc: For priests and leaders in the Church, that they may point to Christ and not to themselves.
For married couples, that their love may reflect Christ and his Church.
For those caught in jealousy and rivalry.
For brothers and sisters who sin, that they may be restored by our prayer.
For our group, that Christ may increase among us.
pm.close: Lord God, John the Baptist rejoiced to hear the Bridegroom's voice. Free us from jealousy and idols, and let your Son increase in our lives. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God has spoken his final Word in his Son.
The kingdom has come near: repent and believe.
Jesus calls ordinary people at work: follow me.
2027-01-11.action: Let go of one thing that holds you back from following Jesus.
2027-01-11.question: What are the nets I find hard to leave?

family.explain: Jesus saw fishermen working by the lake. He said: come, follow me! They left their nets and went with him.
family.intention: We pray for young people thinking about becoming priests or sisters.
family.ask: Ask: “How can our family follow Jesus this week?”

illus: An illustration

A software engineer in Bengaluru began spending his lunch break once a week visiting patients at a nearby hospital. Five years later he left his job to join a religious congregation. He said: Jesus did not call me out of nowhere; he called me in the middle of my ordinary days.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Word of the Father, you call people at their work. Call us too, and give us courage to follow. Amen.
share: God has spoken to us by a Son (Hebrews 1:2). How do I listen to the Son?
Repent, and believe in the good news (Mark 1:15). What good news do I need to believe today?
They left their nets and followed him (Mark 1:18). What nets hold me back?
interc: For the Church at the start of Ordinary Time, that she may follow Christ faithfully.
For vocations to priesthood and religious life.
For fishermen and all who work with their hands.
For those who hesitate to follow Christ.
For our group, that we may listen to the Son.
pm.close: Father, you have spoken your final Word in your Son. Help us to listen, to repent and to follow him in our ordinary days. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jesus teaches with his own authority.
His word drives out evil.
Crowned with glory, he calls us brothers and sisters.
2027-01-12.action: Obey one teaching of Jesus you have been ignoring.
2027-01-12.question: Does Jesus' word have real authority in my decisions?

family.explain: Jesus taught in the synagogue, and everyone was amazed. A man had an evil spirit, and Jesus commanded it to leave. The man was free!
family.intention: We pray for people who are troubled or afraid.
family.ask: Ask: “Which words of Jesus do we want to obey this week?”

illus: An illustration

A young man in Kochi struggling with gambling joined a parish recovery group. They read a Gospel passage at every meeting. He said: when I read that the unclean spirit obeyed Jesus, I understood that my addiction is not stronger than him. He has been free for three years.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you teach with authority and set people free. Teach us now, and free us from all that binds us. Amen.
share: He taught them as one having authority (Mark 1:22). Does Jesus' word guide my choices?
Be silent, and come out of him! (Mark 1:25). What do I need to be freed from?
He is not ashamed to call them brothers and sisters (Hebrews 2:11). How does it feel to be Jesus' brother or sister?
interc: For preachers and teachers, that they may speak Christ's word faithfully.
For those bound by addiction, fear or evil.
For those who feel unworthy of God's love.
For the suffering, that they may see Jesus crowned through suffering.
For our group, that Jesus' word may have authority among us.
pm.close: Father, your Son speaks with authority and frees us from evil. Make us obedient to his word and glad to be his brothers and sisters. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jesus lifts up the sick woman, and she serves.
He prays alone before dawn.
Tested like us, he is able to help us.
2027-01-13.action: Give the first ten minutes of tomorrow morning to prayer.
2027-01-13.question: Where is the deserted place where I meet God each day?

family.explain: Jesus healed Peter's mother-in-law, and she got up and served everyone. Early the next morning Jesus went to a quiet place to pray.
family.intention: We pray for the sick in our family and neighbourhood.
family.ask: Ask: “When can our family pray together quietly each day?”

illus: An illustration

A busy mother of four in Kottayam rises fifteen minutes before her household every morning. She sits by the window with her Bible and a cup of tea. She says: if I do not start with Jesus, the day runs over me; if I do, I can run the day.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you went out before dawn to pray. Draw us into your prayer now, and lift us up as you lifted the sick. Amen.
share: He took her by the hand and lifted her up (Mark 1:31). From what do I need Jesus to lift me?
In the morning he went out and prayed (Mark 1:35). How do I protect time for prayer?
He was tested and can help those who are tested (Hebrews 2:18). What test am I facing?
interc: For the sick and those who care for them.
For those who serve in hidden ways after being healed.
For all who struggle to find time to pray.
For those afraid of death, that Christ may free them.
For our group, that our prayer may be faithful.
pm.close: Father, your Son healed the sick and prayed in the night. Lift us up, teach us to pray, and help us in every test. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Today, do not harden your hearts.
Jesus, moved with pity, touches the leper.
He takes the outcast's place outside.
2027-01-14.action: Send a message of encouragement in faith to someone struggling.
2027-01-14.question: Is my heart soft or hard toward God's voice today?

family.explain: A man with a skin disease begged Jesus for help. Jesus felt sorry for him, touched him and healed him.
family.intention: We pray for people who are left out by others.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone at school or work who is left alone? How can we be kind?”

illus: An illustration

St Devasahayam (Neelakanta Pillai) was a respected official in eighteenth-century Travancore. After his Baptism he refused to treat anyone as untouchable and shared meals with people of every caste. This scandalised many. He accepted imprisonment and death rather than deny Christ. Pope Francis canonised him in 2022, the first Indian layman to be declared a saint.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, today we hear your voice. Soften our hearts, and move us with your pity for the suffering. Amen.
share: Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts (Hebrews 3:7–8). Where is my heart hard?
Exhort one another every day (Hebrews 3:13). Whom can I encourage today?
Moved with pity, Jesus touched him (Mark 1:41). Whom am I afraid to touch?
interc: For people with leprosy and all who are excluded.
For Christians in India, through the prayers of St Devasahayam.
For those who have hardened their hearts against God.
For those who encourage others in faith.
For our group, that we may encourage one another daily.
pm.close: Father, your Son was moved with pity and touched the outcast. Keep our hearts soft to your voice, and give us his compassion for all. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Four friends carry the paralytic to Jesus.
Jesus forgives sins first.
He has authority on earth to forgive.
2027-01-15.action: Bring someone to Jesus this week.
2027-01-15.question: Whom am I carrying to Jesus by my faith?

family.explain: Four friends carried a man who could not walk. The house was full, so they made a hole in the roof and let him down to Jesus! Jesus forgave his sins and healed him.
family.intention: We pray for a friend who needs Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “Which friend can we pray for and help to know Jesus?”

illus: An illustration

A group of four college friends in Thrissur noticed that one of their classmates had stopped coming to classes and was sinking into depression. They took turns visiting him, studying with him and finally brought him to a retreat. He says: I could not walk to God myself; they carried me through the roof.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you saw the faith of the four friends. Look at our faith as we gather, and forgive and heal us. Amen.
share: When Jesus saw their faith (Mark 2:5). Whose faith has carried me?
Son, your sins are forgiven (Mark 2:5). Do I believe Jesus forgives me?
Let us make every effort to enter that rest (Hebrews 4:11). What keeps me from God's rest?
interc: For those who are paralysed by sin, fear or illness.
For friends who carry others to Christ.
For priests who hear confessions.
For those who have not received the sacrament of Reconciliation for many years.
For our group, that our faith may carry others.
pm.close: Father, your Son has authority to forgive sins. Forgive us, raise us up, and make us friends who carry others to him. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God's word is living and sees the heart.
Jesus calls Levi and eats with sinners.
We approach the throne of grace with boldness.
2027-01-16.action: Share a meal or tea with someone others look down on.
2027-01-16.question: Do I see the Church as a hospital for sinners, including me?

family.explain: Levi was a tax collector, and people did not like him. Jesus said: follow me! Then Jesus ate with Levi and his friends. Jesus came to help those who need him.
family.intention: We pray for people who feel others look down on them.
family.ask: Ask: “Who could we invite to our home or our table?”

illus: An illustration

A parish in Ernakulam began a monthly Sunday lunch to which everyone was invited: families, migrant workers, a few men from the bus stand. At first some parishioners grumbled. A year later one of the men from the bus stand was serving at the tables. The parish priest said: this is what Jesus did at Levi's house.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, your word is living and active. Speak to our hearts as we gather, and welcome us as you welcomed Levi. Amen.
share: The word of God is living and active (Hebrews 4:12). What has God's word shown me lately?
Follow me (Mark 2:14). What is my tax booth?
Approach the throne of grace with boldness (Hebrews 4:16). Do I come to God with confidence?
pm.resp: Lord, have mercy on us sinners.
interc: For the Church, that she may be a home for sinners.
For tax collectors, officials and all handling public money, that they may be honest.
For those who feel unworthy of God.
For priests in the confessional, ministers of the throne of grace.
For our group, that we may welcome all as Jesus did.
pm.close: Father, your Son called Levi and ate with sinners. Let your word search our hearts and your mercy heal them. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Christ the High Priest learned obedience through suffering.
While the Bridegroom is present, his friends rejoice.
New wine needs fresh wineskins.
2027-01-18.action: Pray the Our Father daily this week for Christian unity.
2027-01-18.question: Is my heart a fresh wineskin for Christ's new wine?

family.explain: Jesus said: you cannot put new juice into an old dry bottle; it will burst! Jesus brings something new, and we need new hearts.
family.intention: We pray that all Christians may be one family.
family.ask: Ask: “Do we know Christians of other churches? Let us pray for them.”

illus: An illustration

In Thiruvananthapuram, Catholic, Orthodox, Marthoma and CSI youth groups began cleaning a public beach together each January during the unity week. A girl said: we cannot yet share one altar, but we can share one broom and one prayer, and Jesus is pleased.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, eternal High Priest, you pour new wine into our lives. Make us new and make us one. Amen.
share: Jesus offered prayers with loud cries and tears (Hebrews 5:7). How do I pray in my suffering?
The wedding guests cannot fast while the bridegroom is with them (Mark 2:19). Do I live with Christian joy?
New wine into fresh wineskins (Mark 2:22). What must be renewed in me?
interc: For the unity of all Christians.
For priests, that they may deal gently with the weak.
For those suffering, that they may unite their cries with Christ's.
For a renewal of joy in the Church.
For our group, that we may become new wineskins.
pm.close: Father, your Son prayed that all may be one. Renew our hearts and heal the divisions among Christians. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God does not forget the love we show.
Hope is a sure anchor fixed in heaven.
The sabbath was made for humankind.
2027-01-19.action: Plan this Sunday as a day of worship, family and rest.
2027-01-19.question: Where is the anchor of my soul fixed?

family.explain: An anchor keeps a boat from drifting away in the wind. Our hope in Jesus is like an anchor that keeps our hearts steady.
family.intention: We pray for people who feel hopeless.
family.ask: Ask: “What can our family do to make Sunday special for God?”

illus: An illustration

Fishermen in Neendakara say the anchor rope must be long and the anchor heavy; in a storm the boat swings but does not drift onto the rocks. A widow there said after a hard year: my boat swung a lot, but my anchor was in heaven. I did not drift.

pm.open: Faithful God, our hope is anchored in you. Steady our hearts as we gather. Amen.
share: God will not overlook your work and love (Hebrews 6:10). What good work have I grown tired of?
A sure and steadfast anchor of the soul (Hebrews 6:19). What steadies me in storms?
The sabbath was made for humankind (Mark 2:27). How do I keep the Lord's Day?
interc: For those who serve the poor and feel tired.
For those who have lost hope.
For a renewed love of Sunday worship in our families.
For Christian unity.
For our group, that we may persevere in faith and patience.
pm.close: Father, you have given us hope as an anchor. Keep us steady in faith and joyful in your day. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Christ is a priest for ever, like Melchizedek.
Jesus grieves over hardness of heart and heals.
Sebastian and Fabian were brave soldiers of Christ.
2027-01-20.action: Defend someone treated unjustly this week.
2027-01-20.question: Where has my heart grown hard?

family.explain: A man had a hand that did not work. Some people did not want Jesus to heal on the sabbath. Jesus was sad that their hearts were hard, and he healed the man.
family.intention: We pray for soldiers, police and all who protect others.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we be brave like St Sebastian?”

illus: An illustration

Across Kerala, St Sebastian's feasts fill streets with processions and arrows decorated with flowers. An old parish priest used to tell children: Sebastian was shot with arrows and survived, then went back to tell the emperor the truth. Real courage is going back to do what is right.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, priest for ever, soften our hearts and make us brave witnesses like St Sebastian. Amen.
share: A priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek (Psalm 110:4). What does Christ's priesthood mean for me?
He was grieved at their hardness of heart (Mark 3:5). Where is my heart hard?
Share in suffering like a good soldier of Christ Jesus (2 Timothy 2:3). Where do I need courage?
pm.resp: Lord, give us hearts of flesh.
interc: For soldiers and police, through St Sebastian.
For the Pope, through St Fabian.
For those with hardened hearts.
For the sick and disabled.
For Christian unity.
pm.close: Father, your Son is priest for ever and healer of hearts. Make us soft toward you and brave in witness. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Christ always lives to intercede for us.
Crowds press to touch him for healing.
St Agnes, a young girl, was strong in Christ.
2027-01-21.action: When anxious, remember: Jesus is praying for me now.
2027-01-21.question: Do I trust that Jesus is interceding for me?

family.explain: So many people came to Jesus that he needed a boat! They all wanted to touch him and be healed.
family.intention: We pray for girls and children everywhere, that they may be safe.
family.ask: Ask: “What do you want to ask Jesus to heal?”

illus: An illustration

St Agnes's name sounds like the Latin agnus, lamb. Each year on her feast two lambs are blessed in Rome, and their wool is woven into the pallium, the stole worn by archbishops. A young girl's faith is carried on the shoulders of the Church's shepherds.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you always live to intercede for us. Hear the prayers we bring, and give us the courage of St Agnes. Amen.
share: He always lives to make intercession for them (Hebrews 7:25). How does it feel to know Jesus prays for me?
All who had diseases pressed upon him to touch him (Mark 3:10). What need draws me to Jesus?
Agnes was faithful though young. What can young people teach me about faith?
interc: For girls and young women, that they may be safe and respected.
For children who suffer exploitation.
For the sick who long to touch Jesus.
For archbishops who wear the pallium.
For Christian unity.
pm.close: Father, your Son always intercedes for us. Through the prayers of St Agnes make us pure, brave and faithful. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: In the new covenant God writes his law on our hearts.
Jesus calls the Twelve to be with him.
He sends them out to proclaim and heal.
2027-01-22.action: Give fifteen quiet minutes to Jesus today, then do one act of service in his name.
2027-01-22.question: Do I spend time with Jesus before I try to work for him?

family.intention: We pray for bishops, the successors of the apostles.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we spend time with Jesus this week?”

The Missionaries of Charity of St Teresa of Kolkata spend an hour in adoration every day before going to the poor. A visitor in Kolkata once asked if that was not wasted time with so much work waiting. A sister answered: without the hour with him, we would have nothing to give them.

share: I will write them on their hearts (Hebrews 8:10). Is God's law written on my heart or only on paper?
He called to him those whom he wanted (Mark 3:13). How has Jesus called me?
To be with him, and to be sent out (Mark 3:14). Which do I neglect: being with him, or being sent?
interc: For bishops, successors of the apostles.
For missionaries and catechists.
For new vocations to serve the Church.
For Christian unity, that the Twelve's faith may unite us.
For our group, that we may pray and serve.
pm.close: Father, in your Son you made a new covenant. Keep us close to him and send us out with his mercy. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Christ entered once for all with his own blood.

2027-01-23.question: Am I willing to be thought foolish for love of Christ?

family.intention: We pray for people who work hard to help others.
family.ask: Ask: “Who works very hard for our family? Let us thank them.”

When St Damien chose to live among leprosy patients on Molokai, some called him foolish and reckless. Some said the priest was either mad or a saint. Years later the Church answered: a saint. The madness of love is wisdom in God's eyes.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, your blood purifies our conscience. Make us clean and generous as we gather. Amen.
share: He entered once for all with his own blood (Hebrews 9:12). What does Christ's sacrifice mean to me?
Purify our conscience from dead works (Hebrews 9:14). What dead works weigh on me?
They said, He has gone out of his mind (Mark 3:21). Do I love generously enough to seem foolish?

For those who give themselves totally to others.
For families who misunderstand a member's vocation.
For Christian unity.
For our group, that our worship may be pure.
pm.close: Father, through the blood of your Son you purify our conscience. Make our worship living and our love generous. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

2027-01-25.action: Pray each morning this week: What am I to do, Lord?
2027-01-25.question: Is there any area of my life still persecuting Christ?

family.intention: We pray for people who are against God, that they may meet Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “Who can we pray for, that Jesus may change their heart?”

A former gang leader from Thiruvananthapuram, now a catechist, tells young people that he once mocked the Church and attacked a priest. In prison a chaplain visited him weekly. He says: that priest was my Ananias; he called me brother when everyone else called me criminal.

share: Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? (Acts 22:7). How do I treat Christ in his Church?
What am I to do, Lord? (Acts 22:10). Do I ask this question?
Go into all the world (Mark 16:15). Where is my mission field?
interc: For the unity of all Christians, on the last day of the Unity Week.
For those who persecute Christians today.
For missionaries in difficult places.
For the newly baptized.
For our group, that we may share the good news.
pm.close: God of unity, you turned Saul into Paul. Turn our hearts, heal the divisions among Christians, and send us as witnesses. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Faith is handed on in families, as with Timothy.
Rekindle the gift of God within you.
Whoever does God's will is Jesus' family.
2027-01-26.action: Use one gift of God that you have neglected.
2027-01-26.question: What gift of God in me needs to be rekindled?

family.intention: We pray for India on Republic Day, and for our grandparents.

A retired teacher in Kozhikode had stopped playing the organ after her husband died. pm.open: Lord, rekindle the gifts you have given us, and make us your family by doing your will. Amen.
share: A faith that lived first in your grandmother (2 Timothy 1:5). Who handed the faith on to me?
Rekindle the gift of God (2 Timothy 1:6). Which gift have I let grow cold?
Whoever does the will of God (Mark 3:35). Do I do God's will?

For grandparents and parents who hand on the faith.
For India on Republic Day: for justice, peace and harmony.
For those who govern.
For our group, that our gifts may serve the Church.
pm.close: Father, through Timothy and Titus you built up your Church. Rekindle our gifts and bless our nation. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Christ's single sacrifice perfects us for all time.
The sower's seed falls on four soils.

2027-01-27.action: Cut back one worry or desire that chokes God's word.
2027-01-27.question: What kind of soil is my heart today?

family.explain: A farmer threw seeds. Birds ate some, some fell on rocks, some in thorns, and some in good soil and grew big. Let our hearts be good soil!

A coconut farmer in Alappuzha explained the parable to his grandson by showing him two seedlings: one planted in cleared soil, the other where weeds had been left. The second was stunted. He said: God's word is like that. If you do not clear the weeds of your phone and your worries, it cannot grow.

pm.open: Lord, sow your word in us, and make us good soil. Amen.

The cares of the world… choke the word (Mark 4:19). What chokes the word in me?
They hear the word and accept it (Mark 4:20). How do I accept God's word?
interc: For preachers and catechists.
For teachers of the young, through St Angela Merici.
For those whose faith has been choked by worries.
For farmers and all who work the soil.
For our group, that we may bear fruit.
pm.close: Father, your Son's sacrifice has made us holy. Let your word bear fruit in us a hundredfold. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Through Jesus we approach God with confidence.
Do not neglect to meet together.
Let the lamp of faith shine, like St Thomas Aquinas.
2027-01-28.action: Spend ten minutes before the Blessed Sacrament.
2027-01-28.question: Is my faith a lamp on the stand or under a basket?

family.intention: We pray for students and teachers, through St Thomas Aquinas.
family.ask: Ask: “How can our family let our faith shine?”

A medical student in Thrissur struggled with doubts after a science lecture. Her chaplain gave her a page from St Thomas Aquinas on faith and reason. She said: I had thought I must choose between my microscope and my rosary. Thomas taught me that both are gifts of the same God.

pm.open: Lord, give us minds that seek you and hearts that adore you, like St Thomas Aquinas. Amen.
share: Let us approach with a true heart (Hebrews 10:22). How do I come to God?
Not neglecting to meet together (Hebrews 10:25). Do I value Sunday Mass?
A lamp… on the lampstand (Mark 4:21). Where should my faith shine?
pm.resp: Lord, let your light shine in us.
interc: For theologians and teachers of the faith.
For students preparing for examinations.
For those troubled by doubts.
For all who adore the Blessed Sacrament.
For our group, that we may encourage one another.
pm.close: Father, you gave St Thomas wisdom and humility. Enlighten our minds and kindle our love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

The seed grows by itself; God gives the growth.
The mustard seed becomes a great shrub.
2027-01-29.action: Keep going with one good thing you are tempted to give up.
2027-01-29.question: Where am I tempted to shrink back?

A widow in Kottayam ran a tiny Sunday school class of four children in her verandah for twenty years. She never saw big results. At her funeral three priests and two religious sisters came; all had been in her class. One said: she planted a mustard seed and slept; God made it grow.

pm.open: Lord, give us patience and endurance as we sow the seed of your Kingdom. Amen.
share: Do not abandon that confidence of yours (Hebrews 10:35). Where am I losing heart?
He does not know how (Mark 4:27). Do I trust God with what I cannot see?
The smallest of all the seeds (Mark 4:31). What small thing can I offer?

For parents and teachers who sow faith in children.
For persecuted Christians who need endurance.
For farmers awaiting the harvest.
For our group, that we may persevere.
pm.close: Father, you give the growth. Make us faithful sowers and patient waiters. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Faith is the assurance of things hoped for.
Abraham set out not knowing where he was going.
Jesus calmed the storm: Why are you afraid?
2027-01-30.action: Hand your current storm to Jesus in prayer.
2027-01-30.question: Do I believe Jesus cares when he seems asleep?

family.intention: We pray for those going through hard times.

illus: An illustration

During the 2018 floods in Kerala, a family in Chengannur spent two nights on their roof. The grandmother kept saying the words of Jesus: Peace! Be still! When a fishing boat from the coast rescued them, the fishermen told them they had come because they could not sit still at home. She said: the Lord was in that boat too.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are in our boat. Calm our fears and increase our faith. Amen.
share: Faith is the assurance of things hoped for (Hebrews 11:1). What do I hope for?
He set out, not knowing where he was going (Hebrews 11:8). What step is God asking of me?
Why are you afraid? (Mark 4:40). What fear do I need to give to Jesus?
interc: For those in the storms of illness, debt or grief.
For fishermen and sailors at sea.
For refugees and migrants who set out not knowing where they go.
For those who feel God is asleep.
For our group, that we may trust like Mary.
pm.close: Father, your Son calmed the storm. Calm our hearts and deepen our faith, through the prayers of the Virgin Mary. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a happy and holy new year to you all. The Church begins the year by looking at a mother and her child. On the eighth day of Christmas we celebrate Mary, the Holy Mother of God.

Why such a great title? Because of who her Son is. The child she bore is not a man in whom God lived for a while; he is the eternal Son of God who became man in her womb. One Person, truly God and truly man. That is why the Council of Ephesus in 431 declared that Mary is Theotokos, Mother of God. When we honour Mary, we are really confessing our faith in Jesus.

St Paul says that when the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman (Galatians 4:4). Time reached its fullness not in an empire or a palace but in a young woman of Nazareth who said yes. And the purpose of it all is that we might receive adoption as children. Because Mary's Son became our brother, we can call God Abba, Father.

In the Gospel the shepherds hurry to Bethlehem and tell everyone what the angels had said. All who heard were amazed. But Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart (Luke 2:19). Amazement passes; pondering stays. Mary teaches us not to rush from one event to the next, but to keep God's deeds in our heart and seek their meaning.

On the eighth day the child receives his name: Jesus, the Lord saves. The first reading gives us the blessing that God told Aaron to place on the people: the Lord bless you and keep you; the Lord make his face shine upon you; the Lord give you peace (Numbers 6:24–26). In Jesus, God's face has shone upon us; in Jesus, God's peace has a name.

So let us begin this year with Mary. Let us ponder each day what God is doing. Let us call on the holy name of Jesus. And let us be people of peace, for today is also the World Day of Peace. Holy Mary, Mother of God, pray for us this year. Amen.
kids: Children, today we say Happy New Year to Mother Mary! She is the Mother of Jesus, and Jesus is God, so she is the Mother of God.
Mary kept everything about Jesus in her heart. Tonight, before you sleep, tell Jesus one good thing that happened today.

intro: On the eighth day the Child received the name Jesus, which means “the Lord saves”. We begin the year by calling on that name.

sub: The angel chose it before his birth (Matthew 1:21).
His name tells us his mission.

sub: He humbled himself to the cross.

sub: A year lived in his name.

Whatever this year holds, we face it in his name.
opts.resolve: This year I will begin and end each day by calling on the name of Jesus.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, a blessed new year to all of you. On the eighth day after his birth the Child was circumcised and was called Jesus, the name given by the angel before he was conceived (Luke 2:21). The name means the Lord saves. God chose it himself.

In the Bible a name is a mission. The angel told Joseph: you are to name him Jesus, for he will save his people from their sins (Matthew 1:21). Every time we say the name of Jesus, we confess what he came to do.

Paul tells us that because Jesus humbled himself to the cross, God gave him the name that is above every name, so that at the name of Jesus every knee should bend (Philippians 2:9–10). That is why we bow our heads at his name.

Peter, standing before the council, said: there is salvation in no one else, for there is no other name under heaven by which we must be saved (Acts 4:12). We do not know what this year will bring. But we know the name in which we will face it.

So let us begin the year as the Church begins it: in the name of Jesus. Let it be the first word on our lips in the morning and the last at night. And may the Lord bless us and keep us in his name throughout this year. Amen.

opts.a: Mary, Mother of God, and the year ahead
intro: In 431 the Council of Ephesus proclaimed Mary Theotokos, Mother of God. The first day of the year belongs to her and to her Son.

sub: Not mother of a man only.
The Son she bore is God.
Ephesus defended Christ by honouring Mary.
points.apply: Pray the Hail Mary slowly today, weighing the words “Mother of God”.

sub: Mary keeps it in her heart.
A heart that remembers God's deeds.
points.apply: Each night this year, recall one thing God did that day.

sub: So that we might be children.
points.apply: Put your family under Mary's protection for the year.

concl: Mary, Mother of God, is also our mother.
With her we begin the year pondering God's works in our hearts.
opts.resolve: I will entrust this year to Mary, Mother of God, and keep a habit of thanksgiving each night.
homily: Dear friends, today the Church greets Mary with her greatest title: Mother of God. In the year 431 the bishops gathered at Ephesus defended this title, because the Child she bore is not a man who later became God, but the eternal Son of God made man. Honouring Mary protects the truth about Jesus.
Paul says: when the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman (Galatians 4:4). God did not come among us from nowhere. He came through a mother, through a family, through a people.

When the shepherds told what they had seen, Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart (Luke 2:19). She did not understand everything, but she kept it and turned it over in prayer. That is a good way to live a year.
Paul adds: because you are children, God has sent the Spirit of his Son into our hearts, crying, Abba, Father (Galatians 4:6). Through Mary's Son we become children of God.

So let us begin the year with her. Let us ask Mary, Mother of God, to keep our families, and let us learn from her to ponder each day what God has done. And may the Lord bless us and keep us, and give us peace. Amen.

Dear brothers and sisters, today is our feast. At Christmas Jesus was shown to the shepherds of Israel. Today, at the Epiphany, he is shown to the nations. The Magi from the East represent all of us who were not born into the people of Israel, and who have been invited into God's family.

Isaiah had seen it long before: arise, shine; for your light has come… nations shall come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your dawn (Isaiah 60:1, 3). St Paul calls it a mystery hidden for ages: the Gentiles are fellow heirs, members of the same body, sharers in the promise (Ephesians 3:6). In Christ there are no outsiders.

Look at how the Magi find Jesus. First they follow a star; they read God's book of creation honestly. But the star brings them only to Jerusalem. There they need the Scriptures: the prophet Micah says Bethlehem. Reason and faith work together. A sincere mind, open to God's word, finds Christ.

But notice the others. The chief priests and scribes knew the exact verse, yet none of them walked the few hours to Bethlehem. Herod heard the same news and was afraid. Knowledge without worship leaves us where we are; fear of losing our power makes us enemies of Christ. Each of us must ask: am I a seeker, a spectator, or a Herod?

When the Magi see the child with Mary his mother, they kneel and pay him homage, and they open their treasures: gold for a king, frankincense for God, myrrh for one who would die. Adoration is the end of the journey. And then, warned in a dream, they leave for their own country by another road (Matthew 2:12). No one who truly meets Christ goes back the same way.

Today the Church announces the date of Easter: this year 28 March. The star of Bethlehem points to the Cross and the empty tomb. Let us bring Christ our gifts, kneel before him in the Eucharist, and go home this week by another road. Amen.
kids: Children, the wise men followed a star for a long, long way to find Jesus. When they found him, they knelt and gave him gifts.
What gift can you give Jesus? A kind word, a prayer, sharing your toys. Jesus loves your gifts!

intro: The Fathers saw in the three gifts a confession of faith: gold for a king, incense for God, myrrh for one who would die.

sub: The Magi ask for the king of the Jews.

Kneel in adoration before the Blessed Sacrament this week.

The crib already points to the cross.
points.apply: Offer one hidden suffering to Christ.

concl: The Magi confessed Christ as King, God and Saviour.
Our gifts are our obedience, our worship and our sacrifices.
opts.resolve: This week I will bring Christ the gold of obedience, the incense of prayer and the myrrh of a hidden sacrifice.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, the Magi opened their treasure chests and offered him gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh (Matthew 2:11). The Fathers of the Church saw in these three gifts a whole creed.

Gold is for a king. The Magi asked: where is the child who has been born king of the Jews? (Matthew 2:2). Herod trembled for his throne, but Christ's kingship does not compete with earthly power; it reigns by serving.
Incense is for God. The Magi knelt down and paid him homage. Incense rises like prayer, and worship belongs to God alone. These foreign scholars recognised in a little child the God they had sought.
Myrrh is for burial. It was a strange gift for a baby, yet Nicodemus would bring myrrh to bury the body of Jesus (John 19:39). From the crib, the shadow of the cross is already present.
What shall we bring? The gold of obedience, the incense of prayer at the Mass, and the myrrh of a sacrifice offered in love. Then we too, like the Magi, will go home by another road. Amen.

intro: The Magi saw, set out, sought, found, worshipped and returned by another road. Their journey is the journey of every believer.

sub: A star is not enough without a journey.
points.apply: Take one step in faith you have been postponing.
Read the Gospel of the day each morning this week.

sub: They do not return to Herod.
points.apply: Change one habit after meeting Christ at the Mass.

concl: God guides seekers by many lights, and finally by his word.
No one who truly meets Christ goes home by the same road.
opts.resolve: This week I will take one step toward Christ, and change one road that leads me away from him.
homily: Dear friends, the Magi were not Jews and had no Bible. They had a star. God spoke to them in the language they understood, and they set out (Matthew 2:1–2). Faith always begins with a journey.

But the star brought them only as far as Jerusalem. There they needed the Scriptures: in Bethlehem of Judea, for so it has been written by the prophet (Matthew 2:5). God leads us by many lights, but finally by his word.
When they found the Child with Mary his mother, they knelt and worshipped. The long search ended in adoration. Every Sunday at the Mass our search ends in the same way: we kneel before him.
And then: having been warned in a dream not to return to Herod, they left for their own country by another road (Matthew 2:12). After meeting Christ, they could not go back the old way.
Let us ask ourselves: what is my star? Where do I need the Scriptures to guide me? And which old road must I leave after meeting Christ today? Amen.

Dear friends, after feeding the five thousand, Jesus sends his disciples ahead in the boat and goes up the mountain to pray (Mark 6:45–46). Even after a great success, he goes to the Father in prayer.

In the night the disciples are straining at the oars, for the wind is against them. Mark tells us that Jesus saw them (Mark 6:48). From the mountain, in the dark, he sees them. He sees you too, when life is hard work against the wind.

Early in the morning he comes walking on the sea. They think it is a ghost and cry out. Then he says: take heart, it is I; do not be afraid (Mark 6:50). The words it is I are the name of God revealed to Moses. The Lord of the sea climbs into their little boat, and the wind ceases.

Yet Mark says their hearts were hardened; they did not understand about the loaves. We too can see many signs of God's love and still be afraid. St John gives the remedy: there is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear (1 John 4:18).

Today, in many places, the Church celebrates the Epiphany, and our Eastern brothers and sisters celebrate the Baptism of the Lord. Christ is revealed as the one who comes to us in every storm. Let us invite him into our boat, and let his love drive out our fear. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus walked on the water to help his friends in the storm. When you are scared, say: Jesus, I trust in you! He is always near.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today the Christmas season ends at the river Jordan. Mark tells the story in a few lines. John the Baptist says: the one who is more powerful than I is coming after me; I have baptized you with water, but he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit (Mark 1:7–8).

Then Jesus comes from Nazareth and is baptised. As he comes up out of the water, he sees the heavens torn apart and the Spirit descending like a dove on him. And a voice from heaven says: you are my Son, the Beloved; with you I am well pleased (Mark 1:10–11). Father, Son and Holy Spirit are revealed together.

Isaiah described this Servant long before: here is my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen, in whom my soul delights; I have put my spirit upon him (Isaiah 42:1). He will not break a bruised reed. He will be a light to the nations and open the eyes of the blind.

In the second reading Peter sums up Jesus' whole life in one sentence: God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and with power; he went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil (Acts 10:38). That anointing began at the Jordan. And Peter says this to a Roman family: the grace of the Jordan is for every nation.
Why was the sinless Jesus baptised? To stand with sinners and to make the waters holy for us. In our Baptism the heavens opened over us too, and the Father said: you are my beloved child.
So today let us renew our baptismal promises with all our heart. Let us find out the date of our Baptism. And let us go about doing good this week, as people anointed by the Spirit. Amen.
kids: Children, today Jesus was baptised in the river. The Holy Spirit came like a dove and God said: you are my beloved Son!
When you were baptised, God said: you are my beloved child. Ask your parents to show you your Baptism photos!

intro: Isaiah prayed: “O that you would tear open the heavens and come down.” At the Jordan the prayer is answered.

points.apply: Thank God for coming close to you.
Make the sign of the cross slowly and with faith today.

sub: He sanctifies the water for us.
points.apply: Bless yourself with holy water when you enter church.

concl: At the Jordan heaven opens and the Trinity is revealed.
In Baptism heaven opened for us too.
opts.resolve: I will make the sign of the cross with faith, remembering that heaven opened at my Baptism.
homily: Dear friends, long ago Isaiah cried out: O that you would tear open the heavens and come down (Isaiah 64:1). Israel longed for God to come close. At the Jordan the prayer is answered: as Jesus came up from the water, he saw the heavens torn apart and the Spirit descending like a dove on him (Mark 1:10).

This is the great manifestation of the Trinity. The Son stands in the water, the Spirit descends, and the Father's voice says: this is my Son, the Beloved, with whom I am well pleased (Matthew 3:17). Every time we make the sign of the cross, we confess what was revealed at the Jordan.
Jesus did not need to be cleansed. The Fathers said: he went into the water not to be made holy by it, but to make the waters holy for us. From that day, water became the doorway into God's life.

Paul says: he saved us through the water of rebirth and renewal by the Holy Spirit (Titus 3:5). What happened at the Jordan happened to us at the font. Heaven opened over us; the Father called us his children.
Today let us thank God for our Baptism, make the sign of the cross with faith, and come to the Mass as children of an open heaven. Amen.

intro: Most of us were baptised as infants and remember nothing. Today the Church asks us to remember what God did.

points.apply: Find out the date of your Baptism and celebrate it.
Live one day this week as if wearing your baptismal garment.

sub: The candle lit from the Easter flame.
points.apply: Renew your baptismal promises tonight: I reject sin; I believe.

concl: Baptism is not only a past event but a present identity.
We live as children of God, clothed with Christ, walking in the light.
opts.resolve: This week I will find my Baptism date, thank my godparents, and renew my baptismal promises.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, most of us were baptised as infants. We do not remember the water, the oil or the candle. Today, as we celebrate the Lord's own baptism, the Church invites us to remember what God did to us.

Paul asks: do you not know that all of us who have been baptised into Christ Jesus were baptised into his death? We were buried with him by baptism, so that we too might walk in newness of life (Romans 6:3–4). The font is both a tomb and a womb.

He also says: as many of you as were baptised into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ (Galatians 3:27). That is why we received a white garment. We are called to wear Christ every day, at home, at work, in our words.

At Baptism a candle was lit for us, and our godparents spoke promises on our behalf: to reject sin and to believe. Now that we are grown, those promises are ours to keep. Once you were darkness, but now in the Lord you are light (Ephesians 5:8).
So let us find the date of our Baptism, thank our godparents, and tonight renew our promises: I reject sin; I believe in God. Then come to the Mass as children of the light. Amen.

Dear brothers and sisters, the Gospel today shows us how the first disciples came to Jesus. John the Baptist sees Jesus walking by and says: look, here is the Lamb of God! Two of his disciples hear and follow Jesus.

Jesus turns and asks them: what are you looking for? (John 1:38). These are his first words in John's Gospel, and he asks each of us the same question. What are you really looking for? Money, success, love, peace? Behind all our desires is a longing for God.

They answer: Rabbi, where are you staying? And Jesus says: come and see. They went and stayed with him that day. It was about four o'clock in the afternoon (John 1:39). Decades later John still remembered the hour. A real encounter with Jesus changes a life.

Then Andrew finds his brother Simon and says: we have found the Messiah. He brings him to Jesus, who looks at him and gives him a new name, Peter, the rock (John 1:41–42). Faith spreads from person to person.

In the first reading the boy Samuel hears his name called three times and does not understand. Old Eli helps him: say, speak, LORD, for your servant is listening (1 Samuel 3:9). We all need an Eli to help us hear God, and we can be an Eli for someone else.

St Paul reminds us that our bodies are members of Christ and temples of the Holy Spirit. Following Jesus involves the whole of us. This week let us answer Jesus' question honestly, spend time staying with him, and invite one person to come and see. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus asked two friends: what are you looking for? Then he said: come and see! They stayed with him all afternoon and became his friends.
