Andrew brought his brother to Jesus. Who can you bring to church or to pray with you?

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, the first words of Jesus in Mark's Gospel are a summary of everything: the time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has come near; repent, and believe in the good news (Mark 1:15). God's moment has arrived, and it arrives in the person of Jesus.

Two responses are asked. Repent: turn around, change your mind and heart. Believe: trust the good news and give yourself to it. Jonah's few words were enough for Nineveh: the people of Nineveh believed God (Jonah 3:5). How much more should the word of the Son move us.

Then Jesus walks by the sea and calls: follow me and I will make you fish for people. And immediately they left their nets and followed him (Mark 1:17–18). James and John even leave their father in the boat. The word of Jesus is not information; it is a power that changes life.
Paul adds urgency: the appointed time has grown short; the present form of this world is passing away (1 Corinthians 7:29, 31). We may use the things of this world, but we must not cling to them.

Today is the Sunday of the Word of God. Pope Francis asks every Catholic to love the Scriptures. St Jerome said that ignorance of the Scriptures is ignorance of Christ. Let us give the Bible a place of honour in our homes, and read it every day.
The same Jesus who called the fishermen calls us now through his word. Let us leave our nets and follow him. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said to the fishermen: come, follow me! And they went right away. Jesus speaks to us in the Bible.
Can you ask your parents to read a little of the Bible with you every day?

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, Moses promised Israel: the LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people; you shall heed such a prophet (Deuteronomy 18:15). For centuries Israel waited.

In today's Gospel that prophet walks into the synagogue at Capernaum. The people were astounded at his teaching, for he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes (Mark 1:22). The scribes quoted others; Jesus speaks as God's own Word.
Then a man with an unclean spirit cries out: I know who you are, the Holy One of God. Jesus says: be silent, and come out of him! And the spirit leaves (Mark 1:24–26). His word does what it says.
The people ask: what is this? A new teaching, with authority! (Mark 1:27). That same word is spoken to us at every Mass. It can free us from fear, from sin, from addiction, from all that binds.

The Psalm says: O that today you would listen to his voice! Do not harden your hearts (Psalm 95:7–8). Paul speaks of unhindered devotion to the Lord. Married, single or consecrated, we are all called to give our hearts to him.
Today we would have honoured St John Bosco, who freed many young people by the word and love of Christ. Let us listen today, and let Jesus set us free. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus spoke and a bad spirit had to leave! Jesus' words are powerful.
Let us listen to Jesus today, and pray for all children, like St John Bosco did.

homily: Dear friends, on the second day of the new year the Gospel asks a simple question: who are you? The priests and Levites come to John the Baptist and ask him this. John first says what he is not: I am not the Messiah, not Elijah, not the prophet (John 1:20–21).

Then he says who he is: I am the voice of one crying out in the wilderness, make straight the way of the Lord (John 1:23). A voice exists to carry a word. John knows that his whole life is to carry Christ to others. That is true humility: not hating ourselves, but knowing that we live for someone greater.

St John in the first reading tells us to let what we heard from the beginning abide in us (1 John 2:24). Many voices around us offer a new gospel. The Church asks us to stay with the faith of the Apostles.

Today we remember Saints Basil and Gregory, two friends from Cappadocia in present-day Turkey. They studied together in Athens, prayed together as monks, and became bishops. They defended the truth that Jesus is truly God and that the Holy Spirit is truly God. Gregory said that in Athens they knew only two roads: the road to church and the road to school.
Let us ask for John's humility and for holy friendships like theirs. Let our words and our lives say: not me, but Christ. Amen.
kids: Children, John the Baptist said: I am only a voice; Jesus is the important one! Today let us help someone to know Jesus.

homily: Dear friends, after the Epiphany the Church follows the light as it spreads. Jesus leaves Nazareth and makes his home in Capernaum, by the Sea of Galilee. Matthew calls this region Galilee of the Gentiles, a border land where Jews and pagans lived side by side.

There Isaiah's words come true: the people who sat in darkness have seen a great light (Matthew 4:16). Jesus does not start in Jerusalem, among the important people. He starts on the margins, where people felt far from God.

His first word is: repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near (Matthew 4:17). To repent means to turn around. God has come close; we must turn to face him. Then Jesus heals every disease and sickness, and crowds come from everywhere.

St John warns us to test the spirits (1 John 4:1). Not every voice that speaks of God leads to God. The test is simple: does it confess Jesus Christ come in the flesh? Does it lead to the Church, the sacraments, love of neighbour?
Let us welcome the light today. Let us turn from one thing that keeps us in darkness. And let us take courage: the one who is in you is greater than the one who is in the world (1 John 4:4). Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus is like a big light that came to people who were in the dark. When we say sorry and do good, we let his light shine in us!

homily: Dear friends, St John today writes the most famous sentence of his letter: God is love (1 John 4:8). Not only does God love; love is what God is, from all eternity: Father, Son and Holy Spirit.

And John tells us where we can see this love: in this is love, not that we loved God but that he loved us and sent his Son (1 John 4:10). Our love is always a reply. Before we ever prayed, God loved us.

In the Gospel Jesus sees a great crowd and has compassion for them, because they are like sheep without a shepherd (Mark 6:34). He first teaches them, feeding their minds and hearts. Then evening comes and they are hungry.

The disciples say: send them away. Jesus says: you give them something to eat (Mark 6:37). They have only five loaves and two fish. Jesus takes them, looks up to heaven, blesses, breaks and gives. Five thousand eat and twelve baskets are left over. Our little in his hands becomes enough.
These are the words of the Last Supper and of every Mass: took, blessed, broke, gave. Let us bring our five loaves today, our time, our money, our talents, and let him multiply them for others. Amen.
kids: Children, the disciples had only five loaves and two fish, and Jesus fed thousands of people! When you share, Jesus can do great things with your little gift.

homily: Dear friends, Jesus returns to Galilee filled with the power of the Spirit, and on the sabbath he goes to the synagogue of Nazareth, as was his custom (Luke 4:14–16). He is handed the scroll of the prophet Isaiah.

He reads: the Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor, to proclaim release to the captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to let the oppressed go free (Luke 4:18). Then he sits down, and every eye is fixed on him.

And he says: today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing (Luke 4:21). Not one day in the future, not only in the past: today. The word of God is alive. When we hear it at Mass, Christ himself is speaking to us.

St John adds: we love because he first loved us. Those who say, I love God, and hate their brothers or sisters, are liars (1 John 4:19–20). The programme of Nazareth, good news to the poor, freedom for captives, must become our programme.

Today we remember St Raymond of Penyafort, who helped ransom Christian captives and spent his life as a confessor, setting sinners free. May the word of God be fulfilled today in us, in love for the poor and in peace with our brothers and sisters. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus read from the Bible and said: today God's promise comes true! When we help the poor and are kind, God's word comes true in us too.

homily: Dear friends, in one of the towns a man covered with leprosy sees Jesus, falls on his face and begs: Lord, if you choose, you can make me clean (Luke 5:12). He does not doubt Jesus' power. He only asks whether Jesus wants to.

Jesus answers first with his hand. He stretches it out and touches him. By the Law, touching a leper made a person unclean. But with Jesus the opposite happens: his holiness flows into the sick man. I do choose. Be made clean (Luke 5:13). Immediately the leprosy leaves him.
Then Jesus sends him to the priest. Healing is not only for the body; the man must be restored to his family and his community. God's mercy always brings us back to belonging.

Luke adds that crowds came to hear and be healed, but Jesus would withdraw to deserted places and pray (Luke 5:16). St John tells us that God has given us eternal life in his Son; whoever has the Son has life (1 John 5:11–12). In Baptism and the Eucharist, the water and the blood, Jesus still touches us.
What is the leprosy you are ashamed to bring to Jesus? Bring it to him in confession. He still says: I do choose. Be made clean. Amen.
kids: Children, nobody wanted to touch the sick man, but Jesus did! Let us be kind to children whom others leave alone.

homily: Dear friends, the disciples of John the Baptist come to him upset: the one you baptised is baptising, and all are going to him (John 3:26). They feel their master is losing out.

John answers with great freedom. No one can receive anything except what has been given from heaven. Then he uses a wedding image: the bride belongs to the bridegroom. The friend of the bridegroom stands and hears him and rejoices greatly at his voice (John 3:29). John is the best man, not the groom.

And he says the sentence that sums up his life: he must increase, but I must decrease (John 3:30). Jealousy is one of the great sicknesses of parishes, families and workplaces. John shows the cure: joy that Christ is loved, even if I am forgotten.

St John's letter ends with confidence and a warning. If we ask anything according to his will, he hears us (1 John 5:14). And: little children, keep yourselves from idols (1 John 5:21). An idol is anything that takes God's place, including my own importance.
Tomorrow we celebrate the Baptism of the Lord, when John baptises Jesus in the Jordan. Let us prepare by letting Christ grow larger in our lives, and our pride grow smaller. Amen.
kids: Children, John the Baptist was happy when people loved Jesus more than him. Let us be happy when our friends do well!

homily: Dear friends, today Ordinary Time begins. It is called ordinary not because it is dull, but because its weeks are numbered in order. It is the time to follow Jesus through his public life.

Hebrews begins with a solemn sentence: long ago God spoke to our ancestors in many and various ways by the prophets, but in these last days he has spoken to us by a Son (Hebrews 1:1–2). The prophets were many voices; the Son is the final Word. He is the reflection of God's glory and the exact imprint of God's very being.
Mark gives us Jesus' first preaching: the time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has come near; repent, and believe in the good news (Mark 1:15). God's time has arrived. We must turn and trust.

Then Jesus walks by the lake and sees Simon and Andrew casting nets, James and John mending nets. Follow me and I will make you fish for people (Mark 1:17). Immediately they leave their nets. Jesus calls them in the middle of their ordinary work.
In these ordinary weeks, let us listen to the Son and let go of one net that holds us back. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus called fishermen to follow him, and they went right away! Jesus calls you too. How will you follow him today?

homily: Dear friends, Jesus enters the synagogue of Capernaum and teaches. The people are astounded, for he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes (Mark 1:22). The scribes quoted others; Jesus speaks in his own name.

Suddenly a man with an unclean spirit shouts: I know who you are, the Holy One of God. Jesus rebukes the spirit: be silent, and come out of him! And the man is set free. Jesus' word does not only inform; it transforms.

Hebrews looks at Psalm 8: what are human beings that you are mindful of them? God crowned us with glory, yet we see so much broken. But we do see Jesus, who for a little while was made lower than the angels, now crowned with glory and honor because of the suffering of death (Hebrews 2:9).

And he is not ashamed to call us brothers and sisters (Hebrews 2:11). The one who commands evil spirits is our brother. Let his word have authority in our lives today, and let us trust him to set us free. Amen.
kids: Children, when Jesus spoke, even evil had to obey! Jesus is very strong, and he is also our brother who loves us.

homily: Dear friends, today's Gospel shows us a full day in the life of Jesus. After teaching in the synagogue he goes to Simon's house, where Simon's mother-in-law is in bed with a fever.

He came and took her by the hand and lifted her up. Then the fever left her, and she began to serve them (Mark 1:31). The first thing she does with her new strength is serve. Healing leads to service.

At sunset the whole town gathers at the door, and Jesus cures many. Then: in the morning, while it was still very dark, he got up and went out to a deserted place, and there he prayed (Mark 1:35). Jesus' busy day rests on his night prayer.

Hebrews tells us why he came so close: he became like us in every respect, so that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest. Because he himself was tested by what he suffered, he is able to help those who are being tested (Hebrews 2:18).
Today we remember St Hilary, who defended faith in Christ even in exile. Let us ask for Jesus' habit of early prayer, and let him lift us up to serve. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus prayed very early in the morning, while it was still dark. Tomorrow, say a little prayer to Jesus as soon as you wake up!

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews quotes Psalm 95 with great urgency: today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts (Hebrews 3:7–8). The people in the wilderness saw God's works for forty years and still turned away. A heart can harden slowly, without noticing.

The remedy is community: exhort one another every day, as long as it is called today, so that none of you may be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin (Hebrews 3:13). We need each other to stay soft toward God.

In the Gospel a leper kneels before Jesus: if you choose, you can make me clean. Mark says Jesus was moved with pity, a compassion felt deep inside. He stretched out his hand and touched him: I do choose. Be made clean! (Mark 1:41).

Then something surprising happens. The healed man tells everyone, and Jesus could no longer go into a town openly, but stayed out in the country (Mark 1:45). The leper goes back into society; Jesus takes his place outside. That is what Jesus does for us all the way to the Cross.

In India today many honour St Devasahayam, who after his Baptism refused to treat anyone as untouchable and gave his life for Christ. Let us hear the Lord's voice today, keep our hearts soft, and love across every barrier. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus felt so sorry for the sick man that he touched him and made him well. Let us be kind to anyone who is left out.

homily: Dear friends, the house in Capernaum is packed. Four men arrive carrying a paralysed friend on a mat. They cannot get near Jesus. So they climb the roof, dig through it and lower their friend right in front of Jesus.
Mark says: when Jesus saw their faith (Mark 2:5). The faith of the friends matters. We are saved as a people, carried by others' prayers and love.

Then Jesus says something unexpected: son, your sins are forgiven. He sees the deepest paralysis. The scribes think: who can forgive sins but God alone? They are right about God. They do not see that God is standing in front of them.
To show his authority, Jesus says: stand up, take your mat and go. And the man walks out before them all. Everyone says: we have never seen anything like this! (Mark 2:12).

Hebrews invites us: let us make every effort to enter God's rest (Hebrews 4:11). Forgiveness is the door. Let us go to confession, and let us be the four friends for someone who cannot reach Jesus alone. Amen.
kids: Children, four friends carried a sick man to Jesus, even through a roof! Jesus forgave him and made him walk. Can you bring a friend to Jesus by praying for them?

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews gives us a strong image: the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword; it is able to judge the thoughts and intentions of the heart (Hebrews 4:12). God's word sees us as we are.

That could frighten us. But Hebrews continues: we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but one who in every respect has been tested as we are, yet without sin. Let us therefore approach the throne of grace with boldness (Hebrews 4:15–16).
In the Gospel Jesus sees Levi at the tax booth. Tax collectors worked for the Romans and were often dishonest. People despised them. Jesus simply says: follow me. And Levi gets up and follows.

Then Jesus eats at Levi's house with many tax collectors and sinners. The Pharisees complain. Jesus says: those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick; I have come to call not the righteous but sinners (Mark 2:17).

The Church is a hospital for sinners. Let God's word show us our sickness, and let us come boldly to the throne of grace for healing. On this Saturday let us also ask Mary, Refuge of sinners, to bring us to her Son. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus called Levi, whom nobody liked, to be his friend. Jesus loves everyone. Let us be friends with someone who has no friends.

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews shows us Christ as our High Priest. Every priest is chosen from among people and can deal gently with the weak, because he too is weak. Christ did not make himself a priest; the Father said: you are a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek.

In the days of his flesh, Jesus offered up prayers and supplications, with loud cries and tears, and although he was a Son, he learned obedience through what he suffered (Hebrews 5:7–8). Our High Priest knows our tears from inside.

In the Gospel people ask why his disciples do not fast. Jesus says the wedding guests cannot fast while the bridegroom is with them. And no one puts new wine into old wineskins; one puts new wine into fresh wineskins (Mark 2:22). Jesus brings something new that needs new hearts.
Today the Week of Prayer for Christian Unity begins. Our divisions are old wineskins. Let us pray with Jesus, that they may all be one, and let us become new wineskins ourselves. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said you cannot pour new juice into an old cracked bottle. Jesus wants to give us new, happy hearts!

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews speaks to tired Christians: God is not unjust; he will not overlook your work and the love that you showed for his sake in serving the saints (Hebrews 6:10). No act of love is forgotten.
Do not become sluggish, but imitate those who through faith and patience inherit the promises, like Abraham. God bound himself by an oath so that we might seize the hope set before us.
We have this hope, a sure and steadfast anchor of the soul, a hope that enters the inner shrine behind the curtain (Hebrews 6:19). Our anchor is fixed in heaven, where Jesus has gone ahead of us.

In the Gospel Jesus says: the sabbath was made for humankind, and not humankind for the sabbath; so the Son of Man is lord even of the sabbath (Mark 2:27–28). God's law serves our life. Let us keep the Lord's Day as a gift, and hold fast to our anchor of hope. Amen.
kids: Children, an anchor keeps a boat from floating away. Hope in Jesus keeps our hearts safe. Hold on to Jesus!

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews tells us of Melchizedek, king of Salem, who brought out bread and wine and blessed Abraham. He appears without father, without mother, without genealogy, and so, resembling the Son of God, he remains a priest forever (Hebrews 7:3).
Christ is a priest not by family descent, but through the power of an indestructible life. And the bread and wine of Melchizedek point to the Eucharist.

In the Gospel Jesus asks: is it lawful to do good or to do harm on the sabbath, to save life or to kill? But they were silent (Mark 3:4). He looked at them with anger, grieved at their hardness of heart, and healed the withered hand.

Today we honour St Fabian, a pope who died a martyr, and St Sebastian, the Roman soldier loved across Kerala, who served Christ before the emperor and gave his life rather than deny him. Let us ask for hearts soft toward God and firm in courage. Amen.
kids: Children, St Sebastian was a brave soldier for Jesus. Be brave too: stand up for a friend who is being teased.

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews tells us something deeply comforting: Christ is able for all time to save those who approach God through him, since he always lives to make intercession for them (Hebrews 7:25). At this very moment the risen Jesus is praying for you.
He offered himself once for all, and now he is the mediator of a better covenant. We never pray alone; we pray inside his prayer.
In the Gospel crowds come from everywhere. All who had diseases pressed upon him to touch him (Mark 3:10). Even the unclean spirits cry: you are the Son of God! But Jesus silences them.

Today we honour St Agnes, a girl of twelve or thirteen who refused to deny her consecration to Christ and was martyred in Rome. She was weak in the world's eyes, but strong because Christ was praying for her. Let us trust his intercession and ask for her courage. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus is praying for you right now in heaven! St Agnes was a young girl who loved Jesus very much and was very brave.

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews recalls God's promise through Jeremiah: I will put my laws in their minds, and write them on their hearts, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people (Hebrews 8:10). The new covenant is written not on stone but on hearts, and it rests on forgiveness: I will remember their sins no more.
In the Gospel Jesus goes up the mountain, like Moses at Sinai, and calls to him those whom he wanted. He appoints twelve, a new Israel.
Why does he call them? To be with him, and to be sent out to proclaim the message (Mark 3:14). First friendship, then mission. The order matters.
The list is surprising: fishermen, a tax collector, a zealot, even Judas. Jesus calls ordinary, imperfect people. He calls you too: first to be with him in prayer, then to go out in his name. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus chose twelve friends. First they stayed with him, then he sent them to help people. Spend time with Jesus, then go and be kind!

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews takes us into the old tabernacle, where the high priest entered the Holy of Holies once a year with the blood of animals. Then: when Christ came as a high priest, he entered once for all into the Holy Place, not with the blood of goats and calves, but with his own blood, thus obtaining eternal redemption (Hebrews 9:11–12).

If animal blood purified the body, how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without blemish to God, purify our conscience from dead works to worship the living God! (Hebrews 9:14).
Today's Gospel is very short. So many people came that Jesus could not even eat. His relatives went out to restrain him, for people were saying: he has gone out of his mind (Mark 3:21).
Total love looks like madness. The One who gave his blood for us seemed foolish even to his own. Let us let his blood purify our conscience, and let us love with a little of his holy madness. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus worked so hard helping people that he forgot to eat! Jesus loves us with all his heart. Let us love others with all our hearts too.

homily: Dear friends, today the Church celebrates a conversion. Saul of Tarsus says of himself: I persecuted this Way up to the point of death, binding both men and women and putting them in prison (Acts 22:4).

On the road to Damascus a great light shone and he heard: Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting me? He asked: who are you, Lord? And the answer: I am Jesus of Nazareth whom you are persecuting (Acts 22:7–8). Jesus does not say my followers; he says me. Christ and his Church are one Body.

Blind, Saul is led into Damascus. There Ananias, a disciple who was afraid of him, calls him brother and says: get up, be baptized, and have your sins washed away, calling on his name (Acts 22:16). Conversion happens within the Church, through a brother, through a sacrament.
The persecutor becomes the apostle. The risen Lord says: go into all the world and proclaim the good news to the whole creation (Mark 16:15). Paul carried that command across the Roman world.
Today the Week of Prayer for Christian Unity ends. Paul, who once divided by violence, wrote about one Lord, one faith, one baptism. Let us pray that every division among Christians may be healed.
No one is beyond conversion. Let us ask Paul's question every day: what am I to do, Lord? Amen.
kids: Children, Saul hurt Christians, but Jesus spoke to him in a bright light and changed his heart. He became St Paul!
Jesus can change anyone. Let us pray for someone who does not know Jesus.

opts.a: Ananias, the disciple who was afraid
intro: Every conversion story has two heroes: the one who is converted, and the one who dares to welcome him. Today we look at Ananias.

points.apply: Tell God honestly what you fear about someone.

points.h: Go, for he is my chosen instrument
points.apply: Pray for someone you have written off.
Welcome a newcomer or a returning Catholic as brother or sister.

concl: Without Ananias there might have been no Paul.
God still needs disciples brave enough to say brother.
opts.resolve: This week I will reach out to one person I have been afraid of or have given up on.
homily: Dear friends, today we celebrate the conversion of Paul. But there is another hero in the story, a quiet disciple in Damascus named Ananias.

The Lord said to him: get up and go to the street called Straight, and look for a man of Tarsus named Saul. Ananias answered honestly: Lord, I have heard from many about this man, how much evil he has done to your saints (Acts 9:11, 13). He was afraid, and he had good reason to be.

But the Lord said: go, for he is an instrument whom I have chosen to bring my name before Gentiles and kings (Acts 9:15). God sees what we cannot see. The man everyone feared was the man God had chosen.
So Ananias went, laid his hands on Saul and said: Brother Saul (Acts 9:17). His first word was brother. Something like scales fell from Saul's eyes, and he was baptised.

Who is the Saul in my life? The person I fear, avoid, or have given up on? Perhaps God is sending me, as he sent Ananias, to say: brother, sister. And let us bring that person to the Mass in our prayer today. Amen.

intro: Saul did not change his zeal, his intelligence or his energy. He changed his centre. Conversion is not becoming someone else but becoming who God meant.

points.apply: Name one thing you are proud of and offer it to Christ.
Make a good confession this week.

sub: Faith in the Son of God who loved me.
points.apply: Pray each morning: Lord, live in me today.

concl: Conversion keeps our gifts but changes our centre.
Paul's zeal became love for Christ and for all peoples.
opts.resolve: Each morning this week I will pray Galatians 2:20: it is Christ who lives in me.
homily: Dear brothers and sisters, what changed when Saul became Paul? Not his intelligence: he remained a brilliant scholar. Not his energy: he remained tireless. Not his zeal: he remained on fire. What changed was the centre of his life.

He writes: whatever gains I had, these I have come to regard as loss because of Christ (Philippians 3:7). His birth, his learning, his religious record, all the things he had been proud of, he now laid at the feet of Christ.

He discovered that if anyone is in Christ, there is a new creation: everything old has passed away; see, everything has become new (2 Corinthians 5:17). This is what happens in every good confession: the old passes, the new begins.

And he could finally say: it is no longer I who live, but it is Christ who lives in me. And the life I now live in the flesh I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave himself for me (Galatians 2:20).

God does not want to destroy our gifts but to set them on the right centre. Let us offer him our pride, make a good confession, and pray each day: Lord, live in me. And receive him in the Mass as Paul's whole life. Amen.

Dear friends, today we honour Timothy and Titus, Paul's faithful companions. Paul writes to Timothy: I am reminded of your sincere faith, a faith that lived first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice (2 Timothy 1:5).

Then he urges him: rekindle the gift of God that is within you; for God did not give us a spirit of cowardice, but rather a spirit of power and of love and of self-discipline (2 Timothy 1:6–7). The gifts of God can grow cold; we must fan them into flame.
In the Gospel Jesus says: whoever does the will of God is my brother and sister and mother (Mark 3:35). Mary is first among those who did God's will, and Jesus opens his family to all who obey.
Today is Republic Day in India. As members of God's family, let us pray for our nation, for justice and harmony among all its peoples, and for those who govern. Amen.
kids: Children, Timothy's grandmother and mother taught him about Jesus. Thank God for your family, and pray for our country today!

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews tells us that the old priests stood day after day, offering again and again the same sacrifices that can never take away sins. But Christ offered for all time a single sacrifice for sins, and sat down at the right hand of God (Hebrews 10:11–12).
A priest who sits has finished his work. By a single offering he has perfected for all time those who are sanctified (Hebrews 10:14). The Mass makes this one sacrifice present for us.

In the Gospel Jesus tells of the sower. Some seed is choked by thorns: the cares of the world, and the lure of wealth, and the desire for other things (Mark 4:19). But on good soil the word bears fruit thirtyfold, sixtyfold and a hundredfold.
St Angela Merici sowed the word in the hearts of young girls. Let us clear our thorns, be good soil, and sow the word for others. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says our hearts are like soil. When we listen to God's word and do it, it grows like a big plant!

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews says that through the blood of Jesus we have confidence to enter the sanctuary, by the new and living way that he opened for us (Hebrews 10:19–20). So let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith.

It adds: let us consider how to provoke one another to love and good deeds, not neglecting to meet together, as is the habit of some (Hebrews 10:24–25). Faith is lived together, especially at Sunday Mass.

Jesus says a lamp is not put under a basket but on the lampstand (Mark 4:21). St Thomas Aquinas let the light of faith shine through his mind. He showed that faith and reason are friends, two lights from one God.
Yet his learning ended in adoration. He wrote the hymns we sing before the Blessed Sacrament. Let us study our faith and kneel before the Lord. Amen.
kids: Children, St Thomas Aquinas was very clever, but he loved Jesus in the Eucharist most of all. Let us learn about our faith and pray to Jesus!

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews speaks to a tired community: recall those earlier days when, after you had been enlightened, you endured a hard struggle with sufferings (Hebrews 10:32). Now they were tempted to give up.
Do not, therefore, abandon that confidence of yours; it brings a great reward. For you need endurance (Hebrews 10:35–36). Faith is a long faithfulness.

Jesus gives two small parables for the discouraged. The seed grows, he does not know how (Mark 4:27). The mustard seed, the smallest of all seeds, becomes a great shrub (Mark 4:31–32). God's Kingdom grows quietly and surely.
Our part is to sow faithfully and to trust. The growth belongs to God. Do not shrink back. Amen.
kids: Children, a tiny mustard seed grows into a big plant! Small kind things we do for Jesus can grow into something big.

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews gives us the definition of faith: now faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen (Hebrews 11:1).

Abraham set out, not knowing where he was going (Hebrews 11:8). He looked forward to the city whose architect and builder is God. Faith is not knowing the whole road; it is trusting the One who calls.

In the Gospel a great storm arises and Jesus is asleep. The disciples cry: teacher, do you not care that we are perishing? He rises and says: Peace! Be still! Then he asks: why are you afraid? Have you still no faith? (Mark 4:38–40).
Jesus asleep in the boat is not indifferent; he is the Lord of wind and sea. With Mary, who believed without seeing, let us trust him in our storms. Amen.
kids: Children, when a big storm came, Jesus said: Peace! Be still! and the storm stopped. When you are scared, say: Jesus, I trust in you!

intro: Theme: “God sent his Son, born of a woman.”
Mary's divine motherhood, our adoption, and God's blessing for the new year.

sub: The child is the eternal Son.
Honouring Mary protects the truth about Jesus.
q: Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign. Look, the young woman is with child and shall bear a son, and shall name him Immanuel.
And why has this happened to me, that the mother of my Lord comes to me?
points.apply: Pray the Hail Mary slowly today, weighing the words “Mother of God”.

sub: Born under the law to redeem us.
q: As a mother comforts her child, so I will comfort you; you shall be comforted in Jerusalem.
But when the fullness of time had come, God sent his Son, born of a woman, born under the law, in order to redeem those who were under the law, so that we might receive adoption as children.
points.apply: Begin each prayer this week with the word “Abba, Father”.

q: The LORD bless you and keep you; the LORD make his face to shine upon you, and be gracious to you; the LORD lift up his countenance upon you, and give you peace.
But Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart.
points.apply: Write one line each night on what God did that day.

concl: Mary gives us Jesus, and Jesus makes us children of the Father.
Let us begin the year with her, blessed and at peace.
2027-01-01.resolve: Bless your family with Numbers 6:24–26 on every first day of the month this year.

intro: Theme: “Nations shall come to your light.”
Christ revealed to the nations; seeking, finding and adoring.

points.h: A light for all the nations
sub: Isaiah's vision of the nations streaming in.
Paul's mystery: the Gentiles are fellow heirs.
q: Arise, shine; for your light has come, and the glory of the LORD has risen upon you.
that is, the Gentiles have become fellow heirs, members of the same body, and sharers in the promise in Christ Jesus through the gospel.
points.apply: Pray for one person who does not yet know Christ.

sub: The scribes know but do not go.
q: Nations shall come to your light, and kings to the brightness of your dawn.
asking, “Where is the child who has been born king of the Jews? For we observed his star at its rising, and have come to pay him homage.”
points.apply: Read one chapter of a Gospel each day this month.

sub: They knelt and paid him homage.
q: May all kings fall down before him, all nations give him service.

When they saw that the star had stopped, they were overwhelmed with joy. On entering the house, they saw the child with Mary his mother; and they knelt down and paid him homage. Then, opening their treasure chests, they offered him gifts of gold, frankincense, and myrrh.
points.apply: Spend fifteen minutes in adoration before the Blessed Sacrament this week.

concl: The star leads to the Child; the Child leads to the Cross and the empty tomb.
Whoever adores Christ cannot go back the same way.
2027-01-03.resolve: Bless your home this week and offer Christ one concrete gift.

intro: Theme: “Take heart, it is I; do not be afraid.”
Christ comes across the storm; love casts out fear.

sub: He sees them in the dark.
q: He will not let your foot be moved; he who keeps you will not slumber. He who keeps Israel will neither slumber nor sleep.
After saying farewell to them, he went up on the mountain to pray.
points.apply: Pray each night this week for those who are struggling.

q: When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; and through the rivers, they shall not overwhelm you; when you walk through fire you shall not be burned, and the flame shall not consume you.
for they all saw him and were terrified. But immediately he spoke to them and said, “Take heart, it is I; do not be afraid.”
points.apply: Repeat “Jesus, I trust in you” when fear rises.

sub: Hearts hardened in spite of signs.
God lives in us when we love.
q: The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? The LORD is the stronghold of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
There is no fear in love, but perfect love casts out fear; for fear has to do with punishment, and whoever fears has not reached perfection in love.
points.apply: Do one act of love toward someone you fear.

concl: The Lord of the sea climbs into our small boat.
Where love lives, fear loses its grip.
2027-01-06.resolve: Pray Psalm 27 each morning this week.

intro: Theme: “You are my Son, the Beloved; with you I am well pleased.”
The Servant anointed at the Jordan, and our Baptism.

sub: He will not break a bruised reed.
q: Here is my servant, whom I uphold, my chosen, in whom my soul delights; I have put my spirit upon him; he will bring forth justice to the nations.
He proclaimed, “The one who is more powerful than I is coming after me; I am not worthy to stoop down and untie the thong of his sandals.
points.apply: Be gentle this week with someone who is fragile.

q: The voice of the LORD is over the waters; the God of glory thunders, the LORD, over mighty waters.
And just as he was coming up out of the water, he saw the heavens torn apart and the Spirit descending like a dove on him.
points.apply: Pray to the Holy Spirit each morning this week.

q: Ho, everyone who thirsts, come to the waters; and you that have no money, come, buy and eat! Come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.
how God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and with power; how he went about doing good and healing all who were oppressed by the devil, for God was with him.
points.apply: Do one deliberate act of kindness each day this week.

sub: We are buried and raised with him.
q: I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and you shall be clean from all your uncleannesses, and from all your idols I will cleanse you.
As many of you as were baptized into Christ have clothed yourselves with Christ.
points.apply: Find your baptismal date and celebrate it this year.

concl: The heavens opened at the Jordan and have not closed.
Live as the Father's beloved, anointed to do good.
2027-01-10.resolve: Renew your baptismal promises today and bless yourself with holy water each day.

intro: Theme: “What are you looking for?… Come and see.”
How disciples are called: listening, seeking, staying, bringing others.

sub: Samuel hears but does not understand.
Eli helps him recognise God's voice.
We need guides, and can be guides.
q: Now the LORD came and stood there, calling as before, “Samuel! Samuel!” And Samuel said, “Speak, for your servant is listening.”
My sheep hear my voice. I know them, and they follow me.
points.apply: Begin your prayer each day with: Speak, Lord.

sub: Behind every desire, a longing for God.
q: When you search for me, you will find me; if you seek me with all your heart,
When Jesus turned and saw them following, he said to them, “What are you looking for?” They said to him, “Rabbi” (which translated means Teacher), “where are you staying?”
points.apply: Write down what you are really looking for and pray about it.

q: O taste and see that the LORD is good; happy are those who take refuge in him.
He said to them, “Come and see.” They came and saw where he was staying, and they remained with him that day. It was about four o'clock in the afternoon.
points.apply: Spend fifteen minutes with Jesus in the Blessed Sacrament this week.

q: I have told the glad news of deliverance in the great congregation; see, I have not restrained my lips, as you know, O LORD.
He first found his brother Simon and said to him, “We have found the Messiah” (which is translated Anointed).
points.apply: Invite one person to Mass or a prayer group.

concl: Every disciple begins with a question and an invitation.
Come and see, stay, and bring someone else.
2027-01-17.resolve: Be an Andrew this week: bring one person closer to Jesus.

intro: Theme: “Repent, and believe in the good news.”
On the Sunday of the Word of God: the word that calls, converts and sends.

q: For surely I know the plans I have for you, says the LORD, plans for your welfare and not for harm, to give you a future with hope.
Now after John was arrested, Jesus came to Galilee, proclaiming the good news of God, and saying, “The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has come near; repent, and believe in the good news.”
points.apply: Live today as God's moment.

q: And the people of Nineveh believed God; they proclaimed a fast, and everyone, great and small, put on sackcloth.

Indeed, the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing until it divides soul from spirit, joints from marrow; it is able to judge the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
points.apply: Read the Gospel of the day every morning.

q: So he set out from there, and found Elisha son of Shaphat, who was plowing. There were twelve yoke of oxen ahead of him, and he was with the twelfth. Elijah passed by him and threw his mantle over him.
And Jesus said to them, “Follow me and I will make you fish for people.” And immediately they left their nets and followed him.
points.apply: Let go of one net that holds you back.

q: The grass withers, the flower fades; but the word of our God will stand forever.
and those who deal with the world as though they had no dealings with it. For the present form of this world is passing away.
points.apply: Give away something you do not need.

concl: The word that called the fishermen calls us today.
Repent, believe, follow, and read the Scriptures daily.
2027-01-24.resolve: Enthrone the Bible at home and read Mark's Gospel this month.

intro: Theme: “O that today you would listen to his voice!”
The prophet like Moses who teaches and frees with authority.

q: The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people; you shall heed such a prophet.
This is my Son, the Beloved; listen to him!”
points.apply: Read the Gospel as God's own voice.

q: For as the rain and the snow come down from heaven, and do not return there until they have watered the earth, making it bring forth and sprout, giving seed to the sower and bread to the eater, so shall my word be that goes out from my mouth; it shall not return to me empty, but it shall accomplish that which I purpose, and succeed in the thing for which I sent it.
They were astounded at his teaching, for he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.
points.apply: Let Jesus' word, not opinion, guide one decision this week.

q: The Spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me, because the LORD has anointed me; he has sent me to bring good news to the oppressed, to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and release to the prisoners;
But Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be silent, and come out of him!”
points.apply: Bring one bondage to Jesus in confession.

q: For he is our God, and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand. O that today you would listen to his voice!
I say this for your own benefit, not to put any restraint upon you, but to promote good order and unhindered devotion to the Lord.
points.apply: Spend five minutes in silence with the Gospel daily.

concl: Jesus is the prophet like Moses, the Word with authority.
His word frees; let us listen today.
2027-01-31.resolve: Read and pray with the Sunday Gospel every day this week.

intro: Theme: “I am the voice of one crying out in the wilderness.”
John points to Christ; Basil and Gregory defend the faith.

sub: John says what he is not.
He says who he is: a voice.
A voice exists for the Word.
q: A voice cries out: “In the wilderness prepare the way of the LORD, make straight in the desert a highway for our God.”
He said, “I am the voice of one crying out in the wilderness, ‘Make straight the way of the Lord,’” as the prophet Isaiah said.
points.apply: Let one conversation today point to Christ.

sub: Stay with the faith of the Apostles.
q: But this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the LORD: I will put my law within them, and I will write it on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
Let what you heard from the beginning abide in you. If what you heard from the beginning abides in you, then you will abide in the Son and in the Father.
points.apply: Read one paragraph of the Creed in the Catechism this week.

q: For the LORD gives wisdom; from his mouth come knowledge and understanding;
He must increase, but I must decrease.
points.apply: Thank God for a friend who strengthens your faith.

concl: We are voices; Christ is the Word.
Faithful to what we heard, humble like John.
2027-01-02.resolve: Pray the Creed slowly each morning this week.

intro: Theme: “The people who sat in darkness have seen a great light.”
The light moves out into Galilee; conversion and discernment.

sub: God begins where people feel far away.
q: I am the LORD, I have called you in righteousness, I have taken you by the hand and kept you; I have given you as a covenant to the people, a light to the nations, to open the eyes that are blind, to bring out the prisoners from the dungeon, from the prison those who sit in darkness.
the people who sat in darkness have seen a great light, and for those who sat in the region and shadow of death light has dawned.
points.apply: Visit or call someone who lives on the margins of your parish.

q: Cast away from you all the transgressions that you have committed against me, and get yourselves a new heart and a new spirit! Why will you die, O house of Israel?
From that time Jesus began to proclaim, “Repent, for the kingdom of heaven has come near.”
points.apply: Go to confession this month.

sub: Not every voice is from God.
Christ in the flesh is the test.
The one in you is greater.
q: I will tell of the decree of the LORD: He said to me, “You are my son; today I have begotten you.
Little children, you are from God, and have conquered them; for the one who is in you is greater than the one who is in the world.
points.apply: Check one religious message against Church teaching before sharing it.

concl: The light that the Magi saw now walks through Galilee.
Turn to it, and test every other light by it.
2027-01-04.resolve: Read Matthew 4 slowly this evening and pray for those in darkness.

intro: Theme: “God is love.”
The compassion of the Shepherd who feeds his flock.

q: I myself will be the shepherd of my sheep, and I will make them lie down, says the Lord GOD.
As he went ashore, he saw a great crowd; and he had compassion for them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd; and he began to teach them many things.
points.apply: Notice one person in need today before they ask.

points.h: You give them something to eat
sub: The disciples want to send them away.
q: But his servant said, “How can I set this before a hundred people?” So he repeated, “Give it to the people and let them eat, for thus says the LORD, ‘They shall eat and have some left.’”
But he answered them, “You give them something to eat.” They said to him, “Are we to go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread, and give it to them to eat?”
points.apply: Give food to a family in need this week.

q: the LORD appeared to him from far away. I have loved you with an everlasting love; therefore I have continued my faithfulness to you.
Beloved, let us love one another, because love is from God; everyone who loves is born of God and knows God. Whoever does not love does not know God, for God is love.
points.apply: Thank God tonight for three signs of his love.

concl: The miracle of the loaves continues at every altar.
Love received becomes love shared.
2027-01-05.resolve: Share a meal with someone in need this week.

intro: Theme: “Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.”
The Anointed One at Nazareth; love of God shown in love of neighbour.

sub: Jesus returns in the power of the Spirit.
He is the Christ, the Anointed.
q: The spirit of the Lord GOD is upon me, because the LORD has anointed me; he has sent me to bring good news to the oppressed, to bind up the brokenhearted, to proclaim liberty to the captives, and release to the prisoners;

“The Spirit of the Lord is upon me, because he has anointed me to bring good news to the poor. He has sent me to proclaim release to the captives and recovery of sight to the blind, to let the oppressed go free,
points.apply: Pray for those who are poor, captive or blind in our town.

sub: Christ speaks when the Scriptures are read.
q: For he is our God, and we are the people of his pasture, and the sheep of his hand. O that today you would listen to his voice!
Then he began to say to them, “Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.”
points.apply: Choose one verse from today's readings and live it today.

sub: We love because he first loved us.
No split between God and neighbour.
q: You shall not take vengeance or bear a grudge against any of your people, but you shall love your neighbor as yourself: I am the LORD.
Those who say, “I love God,” and hate their brothers or sisters, are liars; for those who do not love a brother or sister whom they have seen, cannot love God whom they have not seen.
points.apply: Make peace with one person this week.

concl: The programme of Nazareth becomes our programme.
Today, not tomorrow, God's word wants to come true in us.
2027-01-07.resolve: Do one work of mercy for a poor or imprisoned person this month.

intro: Theme: “Lord, if you choose, you can make me clean.”
The touch of Jesus heals and restores; whoever has the Son has life.

sub: The leper believes in Jesus' power.
He asks only about his will.
q: So he went down and immersed himself seven times in the Jordan, according to the word of the man of God; his flesh was restored like the flesh of a young boy, and he was clean.
Once, when he was in one of the cities, there was a man covered with leprosy. When he saw Jesus, he bowed with his face to the ground and begged him, “Lord, if you choose, you can make me clean.”
points.apply: Pray today: Lord, if you choose, heal me.

sub: He restores the man to the community.
q: Surely he has borne our infirmities and carried our diseases; yet we accounted him stricken, struck down by God, and afflicted.
Then Jesus stretched out his hand, touched him, and said, “I do choose. Be made clean.” Immediately the leprosy left him.
points.apply: Visit a sick person whom few people visit.

q: I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and you shall be clean from all your uncleannesses, and from all your idols I will cleanse you.
And this is the testimony: God gave us eternal life, and this life is in his Son. Whoever has the Son has life; whoever does not have the Son of God does not have life.
points.apply: Go to confession and receive the Eucharist with new faith.

concl: Jesus still says: I do choose.
His touch reaches us in the sacraments.
2027-01-08.resolve: Make a good confession before the Baptism of the Lord on Sunday.

intro: Theme: “He must increase, but I must decrease.”
The joy of the Bridegroom's friend; prayer and freedom from idols.

sub: John is the friend who rejoices.
q: For as a young man marries a young woman, so shall your builder marry you, and as the bridegroom rejoices over the bride, so shall your God rejoice over you.
He who has the bride is the bridegroom. The friend of the bridegroom, who stands and hears him, rejoices greatly at the bridegroom's voice. For this reason my joy has been fulfilled.
points.apply: Married couples: renew your vows in prayer together this week.

q: Not to us, O LORD, not to us, but to your name give glory, for the sake of your steadfast love and your faithfulness.
He must increase, but I must decrease.
points.apply: Praise someone whose success you envy.

sub: He hears us when we ask by his will.
Pray for a brother who sins.
q: you shall have no other gods before me.

And this is the boldness we have in him, that if we ask anything according to his will, he hears us. And if we know that he hears us in whatever we ask, we know that we have obtained the requests made of him.
points.apply: Name one idol in your life and give it back to God.

concl: John's joy is complete when Christ is loved.
Let Christ grow, and every idol shrink.
2027-01-09.resolve: Prepare for the Baptism of the Lord by renewing your baptismal promises tonight.

intro: Theme: “The time is fulfilled… repent, and believe in the good news.”
God's final Word in the Son, and the call to follow.

points.h: God has spoken by a Son
q: I will raise up for them a prophet like you from among their own people; I will put my words in the mouth of the prophet, who shall speak to them everything that I command.

Long ago God spoke to our ancestors in many and various ways by the prophets, but in these last days he has spoken to us by a Son, whom he appointed heir of all things, through whom he also created the worlds.
points.apply: Read one chapter of Mark each day this month.

q: And in the days of those kings the God of heaven will set up a kingdom that shall never be destroyed, nor shall this kingdom be left to another people. It shall crush all these kingdoms and bring them to an end, and it shall stand forever;
and saying, “The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has come near; repent, and believe in the good news.”
points.apply: Make a good examination of conscience tonight.

q: He left the oxen, ran after Elijah, and said, “Let me kiss my father and my mother, and then I will follow you.” Then Elijah said to him, “Go back again; for what have I done to you?”
And Jesus said to them, “Follow me and I will make you fish for people.” And immediately they left their nets and followed him.
points.apply: Let go of one net that holds you back.

concl: Ordinary Time is the time of following.
The Son speaks; let us listen and follow.
2027-01-11.resolve: Read Mark's Gospel day by day through this season.

intro: Theme: “He taught them as one having authority.”
The word that frees, and the brother crowned with glory.

q: so shall my word be that goes out from my mouth; it shall not return to me empty, but it shall accomplish that which I purpose, and succeed in the thing for which I sent it.
They were astounded at his teaching, for he taught them as one having authority, and not as the scribes.
points.apply: Obey one word of Jesus today.

q: what are human beings that you are mindful of them, mortals that you care for them? Yet you have made them a little lower than God, and crowned them with glory and honor.

but we do see Jesus, who for a little while was made lower than the angels, now crowned with glory and honor because of the suffering of death, so that by the grace of God he might taste death for everyone.
points.apply: Offer one suffering today in union with Jesus.

q: I will tell of your name to my brothers and sisters; in the midst of the congregation I will praise you:
For the one who sanctifies and those who are sanctified all have one Father. For this reason Jesus is not ashamed to call them brothers and sisters,
points.apply: Treat a difficult person today as Jesus' brother or sister.

concl: His word has authority over evil.
He is our brother, crowned with glory.
2027-01-12.resolve: Let one teaching of Jesus shape a concrete decision this week.

intro: Theme: “In the morning, while it was still very dark, he got up… and there he prayed.”
Healing that leads to service, prayer that sustains, a priest who understands.

sub: He takes her by the hand.
q: O LORD my God, I cried to you for help, and you have healed me.
He came and took her by the hand and lifted her up. Then the fever left her, and she began to serve them.
points.apply: Serve someone today in thanks for a blessing.

q: O LORD, in the morning you hear my voice; in the morning I plead my case to you, and watch.
In the morning, while it was still very dark, he got up and went out to a deserted place, and there he prayed.
points.apply: Pray before you touch your phone each morning.

sub: He shared our flesh and blood.
He frees us from the fear of death.
He helps those who are tested.
q: He was despised and rejected by others; a man of suffering and acquainted with infirmity; and as one from whom others hide their faces he was despised, and we held him of no account.
Because he himself was tested by what he suffered, he is able to help those who are being tested.
points.apply: Bring your present trial to Jesus by name.

concl: Jesus' power flows from his prayer.
He who was tested lifts us up to serve.
2027-01-13.resolve: Keep a morning prayer time all this week.

intro: Theme: “Moved with pity, Jesus stretched out his hand and touched him.”
Today's call, the compassion of Jesus, and the One who goes outside for us.

q: Do not harden your hearts, as at Meribah, as on the day at Massah in the wilderness,
But exhort one another every day, as long as it is called “today,” so that none of you may be hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.
points.apply: Encourage one person in faith today.

q: The person who has the leprous disease shall wear torn clothes and let the hair of his head be disheveled; and he shall cover his upper lip and cry out, “Unclean, unclean.”
Moved with pity, Jesus stretched out his hand and touched him, and said to him, “I do choose. Be made clean!”
points.apply: Visit someone who is lonely or excluded.

sub: The healed man spreads the news.
q: But he was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities; upon him was the punishment that made us whole, and by his bruises we are healed.
But he went out and began to proclaim it freely, and to spread the word, so that Jesus could no longer go into a town openly, but stayed out in the country; and people came to him from every quarter.
points.apply: Thank Jesus for taking your place.

concl: Today is the day to hear his voice.
Jesus goes outside so that the outcast may come in.
2027-01-14.resolve: Cross one barrier of caste, class or prejudice this week.

intro: Theme: “Son, your sins are forgiven.”
Faith that carries others, forgiveness that heals, rest that God promises.

sub: Four friends dig through the roof.
q: But Ruth said, “Do not press me to leave you or to turn back from following you! Where you go, I will go; where you lodge, I will lodge; your people shall be my people, and your God my God.
When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the paralytic, “Son, your sins are forgiven.”
points.apply: Pray daily this week for one friend far from God.

q: I, I am He who blots out your transgressions for my own sake, and I will not remember your sins.
And he stood up, and immediately took the mat and went out before all of them; so that they were all amazed and glorified God, saying, “We have never seen anything like this!”
points.apply: Go to confession before the end of January.

q: And on the seventh day God finished the work that he had done, and he rested on the seventh day from all the work that he had done.
Let us therefore make every effort to enter that rest, so that no one may fall through such disobedience as theirs.
points.apply: Keep Sunday this week as a true day of rest and worship.

concl: Jesus forgives first, then heals.
Let us be carried, and let us carry others.
2027-01-15.resolve: Bring one friend to Jesus by prayer and invitation this week.

intro: Theme: “I have come to call not the righteous but sinners.”
The word that searches the heart and the mercy that welcomes the sinner.

q: Is not my word like fire, says the LORD, and like a hammer that breaks a rock in pieces?

Indeed, the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing until it divides soul from spirit, joints from marrow; it is able to judge the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
points.apply: Pray with today's Gospel for ten minutes.

q: For I desire steadfast love and not sacrifice, the knowledge of God rather than burnt offerings.
When Jesus heard this, he said to them, “Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick; I have come to call not the righteous but sinners.”
points.apply: Welcome someone others avoid.

sub: Tested as we are, without sin.
q: As a father has compassion for his children, so the LORD has compassion for those who fear him.
Let us therefore approach the throne of grace with boldness, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help in time of need.
points.apply: Go to confession with confidence.

concl: The word shows our sickness; the Physician heals it.
Come boldly: the throne is a throne of grace.
2027-01-16.resolve: Read one Gospel passage each day and let it search your heart.

intro: Theme: “New wine into fresh wineskins.”
The suffering High Priest, the joy of the Bridegroom, the call to newness and unity.

q: For he did not despise or abhor the affliction of the afflicted; he did not hide his face from me, but heard when I cried to him.
In the days of his flesh, Jesus offered up prayers and supplications, with loud cries and tears, to the one who was able to save him from death, and he was heard because of his reverent submission.
points.apply: Bring your tears to God honestly in prayer.

q: The days are surely coming, says the LORD, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and the house of Judah.
And no one puts new wine into old wineskins; otherwise, the wine will burst the skins, and the wine is lost, and so are the skins; but one puts new wine into fresh wineskins.”
points.apply: Let go of one old habit that resists Christ.

sub: So that the world may believe.
q: I will make them one nation in the land, on the mountains of Israel; and one king shall be king over them all. Never again shall they be two nations, and never again shall they be divided into two kingdoms.
that they may all be one. As you, Father, are in me and I am in you, may they also be in us, so that the world may believe that you have sent me.
points.apply: Pray daily this week for Christian unity.

concl: Christ is the eternal High Priest who brings new wine.
Let us become new wineskins, united in him.
2027-01-18.resolve: Do one act of friendship with Christians of another Church during this week.

intro: Theme: “A sure and steadfast anchor of the soul.”
Persevering love, hope anchored in heaven, the Lord of the sabbath.

q: God is not a human being, that he should lie, or a mortal, that he should change his mind. Has he promised, and will he not do it? Has he spoken, and will he not fulfill it?
We have this hope, a sure and steadfast anchor of the soul, a hope that enters the inner shrine behind the curtain,
points.apply: Hold on to one promise of God in a present trouble.

q: He has gained renown by his wonderful deeds; the LORD is gracious and merciful.
For God is not unjust; he will not overlook your work and the love that you showed for his sake in serving the saints, as you still do.
points.apply: Return to one good work you abandoned.

q: Remember the sabbath day, and keep it holy.
Then he said to them, “The sabbath was made for humankind, and not humankind for the sabbath; so the Son of Man is lord even of the sabbath.”
points.apply: Make Sunday a day of worship, family and rest.

concl: God remembers our love and anchors our hope.
Christ is Lord of our time and our rest.
2027-01-19.resolve: Keep next Sunday holy as a family.

intro: Theme: “Is it lawful to do good or to do harm on the sabbath, to save life or to kill?”
The eternal priest, the hardened heart, the brave martyrs.

q: And King Melchizedek of Salem brought out bread and wine; he was priest of God Most High.

It is even more obvious when another priest arises, resembling Melchizedek, one who has become a priest, not through a legal requirement concerning physical descent, but through the power of an indestructible life.
points.apply: Thank Christ the priest at Mass this week.

q: I will give them one heart, and put a new spirit within them; I will remove the heart of stone from their flesh and give them a heart of flesh,
He looked around at them with anger; he was grieved at their hardness of heart and said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He stretched it out, and his hand was restored.
points.apply: Ask God to soften one hard place in your heart.

q: I hereby command you: Be strong and courageous; do not be frightened or dismayed, for the LORD your God is with you wherever you go.”
Share in suffering like a good soldier of Christ Jesus.
points.apply: Defend someone treated unjustly.

concl: Christ the priest heals hardened hearts.
Sebastian and Fabian show the courage of soft hearts.
2027-01-20.resolve: Choose always to do good and save life this week.

intro: Theme: “He always lives to make intercession for them.”
Christ the interceding High Priest; crowds who touch him; Agnes strong in weakness.

q: Therefore I will allot him a portion with the great, and he shall divide the spoil with the strong; because he poured out himself to death, and was numbered with the transgressors; yet he bore the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors.
Consequently he is able for all time to save those who approach God through him, since he always lives to make intercession for them.
points.apply: Pray today: Jesus, I join my prayer to yours.

sub: He heals by his word and touch.
q: he sent out his word and healed them, and delivered them from destruction.
for he had cured many, so that all who had diseases pressed upon him to touch him.
points.apply: Bring one sick person to Jesus in prayer daily.

q: My beloved is mine and I am his; he pastures his flock among the lilies.
But God chose what is foolish in the world to shame the wise; God chose what is weak in the world to shame the strong;
points.apply: Pray for the protection of girls and children.

concl: We never pray alone: Christ intercedes for us.
Like Agnes, the weak become strong in him.
2027-01-21.resolve: Remember daily this week that Jesus is praying for you.

intro: Theme: “To be with him, and to be sent out.”
The new covenant written on hearts; the Twelve called and sent.

q: No longer shall they teach one another, or say to each other, “Know the LORD,” for they shall all know me, from the least of them to the greatest, says the LORD; for I will forgive their iniquity, and remember their sin no more.

This is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the Lord: I will put my laws in their minds, and write them on their hearts, and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
points.apply: Memorise one commandment of love this week.

q: And Moses wrote down all the words of the LORD. He rose early in the morning, and built an altar at the foot of the mountain, and set up twelve pillars, corresponding to the twelve tribes of Israel.
And he appointed twelve, whom he also named apostles, to be with him, and to be sent out to proclaim the message, and to have authority to cast out demons.
points.apply: Give Jesus fifteen quiet minutes today.

q: Steadfast love and faithfulness will meet; righteousness and peace will kiss each other.
For I will be merciful toward their iniquities, and I will remember their sins no more.”
points.apply: Show mercy to someone who wronged you.

concl: First with him, then sent by him.
The new covenant is mercy written on hearts.
2027-01-22.resolve: Pray daily before you serve this week.

intro: Theme: “How much more will the blood of Christ… purify our conscience!”
The once-for-all sacrifice, a purified conscience, the madness of love.

q: He shall slaughter the goat of the sin offering that is for the people and bring its blood inside the curtain, and do with its blood as he did with the blood of the bull, sprinkling it upon the mercy seat and before the mercy seat.

But when Christ came as a high priest of the good things that have come, then through the greater and perfect tent (not made with hands, that is, not of this creation), he entered once for all into the Holy Place, not with the blood of goats and calves, but with his own blood, thus obtaining eternal redemption.
points.apply: Thank Jesus for his blood at the consecration this Sunday.

q: Wash me thoroughly from my iniquity, and cleanse me from my sin.
how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without blemish to God, purify our conscience from dead works to worship the living God!
points.apply: Go to confession soon.

q: O LORD, you have enticed me, and I was enticed; you have overpowered me, and you have prevailed. I have become a laughingstock all day long; everyone mocks me.
When his family heard it, they went out to restrain him, for people were saying, “He has gone out of his mind.”
points.apply: Do one generous act others may find excessive.

concl: Christ's blood cleanses us for true worship.
His love looks foolish, and is the wisdom of God.
2027-01-23.resolve: Make a good confession before the end of January.

intro: Theme: “What am I to do, Lord?”
The persecutor becomes the apostle: grace, the Church, and mission.

q: Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you were born I consecrated you; I appointed you a prophet to the nations.”
for I am the least of the apostles, unfit to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God.
points.apply: Thank God for his patience with your past.

q: Then the LORD called, “Samuel! Samuel!” and he said, “Here I am!”
I answered, ‘Who are you, Lord?’ Then he said to me, ‘I am Jesus of Nazareth whom you are persecuting.’
points.apply: Treat every member of the Church as Christ.

q: I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and you shall be clean from all your uncleannesses, and from all your idols I will cleanse you.
And now why do you delay? Get up, be baptized, and have your sins washed away, calling on his name.’
points.apply: Be an Ananias to someone this week.

q: Praise the LORD, all you nations! Extol him, all you peoples!
And he said to them, “Go into all the world and proclaim the good news to the whole creation.
points.apply: Pray for one Christian community other than your own.

concl: No one is beyond conversion.
Paul's question becomes ours: What am I to do, Lord?
2027-01-25.resolve: Ask Paul's question every morning this week.

intro: Theme: “Rekindle the gift of God that is within you.”
Timothy and Titus: faith handed on, gifts rekindled, God's family, and our nation.

q: One generation shall laud your works to another, and shall declare your mighty acts.
I am reminded of your sincere faith, a faith that lived first in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice and now, I am sure, lives in you.
points.apply: Thank someone who handed the faith on to you.

q: The spirit of the LORD shall rest on him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and the fear of the LORD.
for God did not give us a spirit of cowardice, but rather a spirit of power and of love and of self-discipline.
points.apply: Use one neglected gift this week.

q: But seek the welfare of the city where I have sent you into exile, and pray to the LORD on its behalf, for in its welfare you will find your welfare.
Whoever does the will of God is my brother and sister and mother.”
points.apply: Pray for India and its leaders today.

concl: Faith received must be handed on and kept aflame.
God's family prays and works for the good of the nation.
2027-01-26.resolve: Rekindle one gift in the service of your parish.

intro: Theme: “They hear the word and accept it and bear fruit.”
Christ's single sacrifice, and the soil of our hearts.

q: The LORD has sworn and will not change his mind, “You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.”
For by a single offering he has perfected for all time those who are sanctified.
points.apply: Attend Mass this week knowing it makes Calvary present.

q: Do not wear yourself out to get rich; be wise enough to desist.
but the cares of the world, and the lure of wealth, and the desire for other things come in and choke the word, and it yields nothing.
points.apply: Reduce screen time to make room for Scripture.

q: For as the rain and the snow come down from heaven, and do not return there until they have watered the earth, making it bring forth and sprout, giving seed to the sower and bread to the eater, so shall my word be that goes out from my mouth; it shall not return to me empty, but it shall accomplish that which I purpose, and succeed in the thing for which I sent it.
And these are the ones sown on the good soil: they hear the word and accept it and bear fruit, thirty and sixty and a hundredfold.”
points.apply: Share one verse with a young person, as St Angela did.

concl: Christ's sacrifice is complete; his word is sown.
Let us be good soil and good sowers.
2027-01-27.resolve: Read the day's Gospel every morning this week.

intro: Theme: “Is a lamp… put under the bushel basket?”
St Thomas Aquinas: confident faith, community, and the light that ends in adoration.

q: Who shall ascend the hill of the LORD? And who shall stand in his holy place? Those who have clean hands and pure hearts, who do not lift up their souls to what is false, and do not swear deceitfully.
let us approach with a true heart in full assurance of faith, with our hearts sprinkled clean from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.
points.apply: Prepare for Communion with a short act of contrition.

q: How very good and pleasant it is when kindred live together in unity!
not neglecting to meet together, as is the habit of some, but encouraging one another, and all the more as you see the Day approaching.
points.apply: Invite someone to Sunday Mass.

q: Your word is a lamp to my feet and a light to my path.
He said to them, “Is a lamp brought in to be put under the bushel basket, or under the bed, and not on the lampstand?
points.apply: Read one paragraph of the Catechism each day.

concl: Faith is confident, communal and luminous.
Like Thomas, let our study lead us to adore.
2027-01-28.resolve: Spend time before the Blessed Sacrament this week.

intro: Theme: “The seed would sprout and grow, he does not know how.”
Endurance, patience and the quiet growth of God's Kingdom.

q: Wait for the LORD; be strong, and let your heart take courage; wait for the LORD!
Do not, therefore, abandon that confidence of yours; it brings a great reward.
points.apply: Persevere in one good habit this week.

q: Commit your way to the LORD; trust in him, and he will act.
So neither the one who plants nor the one who waters is anything, but only God who gives the growth.
points.apply: Leave one worry about results with God.

q: On the mountain height of Israel I will plant it, in order that it may produce boughs and bear fruit, and become a noble cedar. Under it every kind of bird will live; in the shade of its branches will nest winged creatures of every kind.
It is like a mustard seed, which, when sown upon the ground, is the smallest of all the seeds on earth;
points.apply: Do one small act of faith and trust God with it.

concl: God's Kingdom grows quietly and surely.
Sow faithfully, endure patiently.
2027-01-29.resolve: Do not give up a good work you have begun.

intro: Theme: “Why are you afraid? Have you still no faith?”
Faith that sets out, and faith in the storm.

q: Trust in the LORD with all your heart, and do not rely on your own insight.
Now faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen.
points.apply: Make an act of faith each morning.

q: Now the LORD said to Abram, “Go from your country and your kindred and your father's house to the land that I will show you.
By faith Abraham obeyed when he was called to set out for a place that he was to receive as an inheritance; and he set out, not knowing where he was going.
points.apply: Take one step of trust God asks of you.

q: He made the storm be still, and the waves of the sea were hushed.
He woke up and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Peace! Be still!” Then the wind ceased, and there was a dead calm.
points.apply: Hand your storm to Jesus in prayer tonight.

concl: Faith trusts the One who calls, not the map of the road.
The Lord is in our boat.
2027-01-30.resolve: Pray “Jesus, I trust in you” whenever you are afraid.
